body:
# Phase directive — «Harness-prefix and identity-floor ledger rows» (Epoch 4, viola-0.2.0; the head entry at `b3eb184c`)

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. Nothing else under it is read, cited or snapped. A fact the
plan needs and this directive does not state is ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

The operator is AWAY from THIS session (he answers through the overseer's dialogs, and he is at hand today): raise
NO question dialog for him. A fork that is his is written to `{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the
options in order with each one's cost, the recommendation marked) and the step stops there, saying so. A technical
fork is answered by the overseer's relay at once. **This phase makes NO live start and reads nothing of the
operator's real `~/.claude*`.** In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## Facts, measured by the overseer 2026-11-20 — cite them as this directive's

- A bare `claude` on this host is 2.1.329 (mise `latest`; 2.1.327, .328 and .329 stand under
  `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/`). THIS session still runs 2.1.328, started before the move.
- The tree at `b3eb184c` holds 27 relied ledger rows and ONE stamped fixture set (2.1.328); 2.1.287, 2.1.302 and
  2.1.325 are drift-only since the last chunk but one, and both default-version constants read 2.1.328. A 27-row
  stamp of 2.1.328 stands in the rig's kept `target/live-rig/question-stamp.json`. PATH's 2.1.329 read verified,
  27 of 27, once, in a scratch home that is gone (the `AV` start of 2026-11-20T16:48:59Z): no stamp of it and no
  fixture set of it stands anywhere.
- The live home's stamp is a 24-row stamp of 2.1.328; the pinned product (the release build of `a59da9da`) holds
  none of the last four mends and is untouched until its re-pin. Call no scheduled-wake or timer tool, and never
  print a compiled screen literal in a chat message.
- The last time a relied row was added (2026-11-20, the 27th), the founder chose: 2.1.328 ALONE re-recorded whole by
  one live `viola verify --record` in the rig's scratch home; no synthetic payload inside a committed recorded set.
  That was his answer for THAT chunk; this chunk's is asked again.
- The documentation leaves hold no figure the code states: this chunk adds none.

## The directive

1. Scope is the route entry and its carries as they stand at `b3eb184c`, nothing wider: the harness-prefix and
   identity-floor ledger rows — a second session sending into a verify child; env NAMES, never values, captured;
   stamped live. The WATCH on `cli_wheel path5_a_turn_left_running_is_cleared_by_pause_then_release` is read at
   each run from the test's own line (a recurrence is read from the job log and the test's own events BEFORE any
   mend; a CI red on it is not re-run before the overseer's word); the rehearsal red is acted on only at its next
   red. Every carry is disposed by name in the plan.
2. **The size risk is what the probe DOES inside verify and what it CAPTURES.** Say at P3, from the code and from
   what can be read with NO start (the installed bundles, verify's runs, the capture arm, the earlier chunks'
   evidence in the store):
   - what each row relies on today without a row (where the product already assumes the harness prefix and the
     identity floor), and what goes wrong for the driver or the human when the assumption fails on a new CLI;
   - **«a second session sending into a verify child» — its exact shape:** which process is the second session,
     how it reaches the child (a viola endpoint, the channel, a paste), what it sends, what the child then shows,
     and what is read to tell the harness-origin prefix; how long it adds to verify, whether it needs a model
     turn, what it leaves in the user's Claude config beyond today's accepted residuals;
   - **the env capture — the private-outward edge:** which variables' NAMES are captured, by which hook or probe,
     where they are written (the stamp, a recorded fixture, a log line), and the proof that NO value can reach
     any file, fixture, stamp, log or screen read — the test that fails if a value is captured, and what the
     `--record` scrub does with a name that itself carries private text (a user-named variable);
   - how many relied rows this adds and what that does to every stamped version and the one stamped fixture set
     — and WHICH versions «stamped live» means: 2.1.328 re-recorded again, 2.1.329 recorded for the first time
     (it reads verified today), or both; in which home (the rig's scratch home; the live home's re-stamp stays
     the re-pin step's);
   - **every master row whose words the change reaches: search ALL seven masters before the block is written**
     (verify's child set and its runs, the capture arm and its closed ids, env reads and the env keep-list, the
     identity floor, the harness prefix, the ledger's rows, the residual rows, what leaves the process) and name
     EVERY reached row, with the ones read as not reached beside them. A widening is said as one HERE, whole. A
     row found reached AFTER the block is a fork of its own — the last two chunks each cost a second founder
     round that way: read the picked rows for the BEHAVIOUR's consequences (what is printed, what is read, what
     is written, who waits), not for the change's own words alone;
   - whether one implement window holds it, or the entry splits and where.
3. **At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block in `founder-forks.md`:** your window; the answer path recommended
   and the ones set aside, each with how it fails; every reached master row; every live start's SHAPE before the
   count — processes, every byte typed, every dialog raised and how it is answered, the stop, every file written
   and where, under WHICH home; for each start a predicate its reading can FAIL, the red reading named; what each
   start READS (key names, counts, closed words — never a text) and from WHERE (a payload value, a transcript, a
   screen, viola's own events); whether any typed key or answered dialog moves the wheel before a send; the
   capability's concretized claim and what «verified» would rest on; a recommended cap and what one spare would be
   for. The cap, any key or byte into a CLI dialog, any widening, what «verified» rests on and any read or write
   under his real home are the founder's: the block WAITS for him.
4. **For every capped start, name what it needs ABSENT or PRESENT on disk outside the tree** (a kept stamp, a kept
   dir, a scratch, a runtime dir), each with a no-start gate entry right before the start, placed so a round
   resumed at one entry still fires it; a start whose product is kept gets an entry that reads it AFTER.
5. One ledger, one count: `--cap` is the RUNNING total of base starts in the ledger file. A census entry after
   the LAST live leg is keyed to the operator leg.
6. Every control stands on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases AND building the whole workspace where the
   case needs a root binary; the bound that applies is the entry's own timeout key, ids within 16 characters.
   Every filter term of a gate entry SELECTS at least one test under its layer flag. An expect atom must be able
   to fail; a word that may honestly read two ways is a READING recorded, not a failing atom. A test that skips
   prints its reason. The plan names operator entries by their run text, never by a number.
7. Before a live round the host is read (`hostwatch.py read --last 15`): a CONTENDED reading with a NEIGHBOUR
   named stops and is re-read, never retried into. The token window is the rig's own check, never a hand read; a
   start refused for it is uncounted — stop and say so.
8. No mutation run. A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned
   user home. Read `df` before a whole rebuild.
9. A fold is decided at the PHASE. A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop
   and tell the overseer. On an account-limit refusal, stop where you are.
10. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool, with any argument. End every process you start; remove no scratch
    clone by a recursive delete — name it on the card instead. An entry that asserts a state a LATER step of the
    same plan ends is keyed to the round leg. Never write that the rig refuses a condition without the line that
    refuses it.
11. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the
    union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY cited row is in the union or its standing
    list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` /
    `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

# P3-block relay — «Harness-prefix and identity-floor ledger rows» (chunk 2026-11-20-harness-prefix-and-identity-floor-ledger-rows)

This relay and the phase directive are the only files of this folder you read or snap. You are in a FRESH window:
re-read your run dir `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-20T18-17-18Z-phase` and its `founder-forks.md` from disk first,
resume the take-up at P4 (the `research` row stands), append the answers below to `founder-forks.md`, snap this
relay, take P4 on them and go on to the P5 card. No live start in this phase; no scheduled-wake or timer tool. In
your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## The founder's own words — given in two dialogs and read at 2026-11-21T05:41:11Z

1. **Fork 1, the split: «Обе строки в этом чанке».** NOT split — he chose your option (b) over the recommended
   split: this chunk takes BOTH rows, `identity-floor` (v2-26) and `cross-session-prefix` (v2-25), 27 → 29. He was
   shown its cost in these words: the second session's path decided now, and a red on the sender holding the
   identity row's stamp too, since one verify stamps both.
2. **Fork 2, the second session's path: «A: claude-отправитель в print-режиме (Recommended)».** Your path (A): one
   more direct child of verify, `claude -p` on Haiku with no session persistence, its one allowed tool the CLI's
   own cross-session send, the compiled prompt naming Run B's session id as the only target; only the raw start
   of the captured prompt read against the four compiled literals, one closed word kept. He was shown, in the
   question's words: two model turns more per verify; that the model can refuse or misaddress, and that in a real
   config the probe text would then land in another live session of the user's — lowered by naming one id, not
   closed, accepted as a residual; that it now also runs under the automatic verify, with no human, in a user's
   real config; and the three premises only a live start measures. This is his ratification of that widening of
   verify's child set and of that residual, over the rows your block's §5 names for it, and nothing wider. Paths
   (B) and (C) are declined: verify reads no CLI credential and sets no floor name.
3. **Fork 3, the env capture: «Да, через рукав захвата (Recommended)».** E1: the existing capture arm reads its
   process's env NAMES, keeps `CLAUDE*` names only, counts the rest, drops every value before any write, removes
   the user's kept names in memory, writes one more 0600 file in the same probe dir; names land in the stamp's
   measured block and, under `--record`, in one fixture through the scrub; no log line, no screen read. His
   ratification of that widening of the capture arm over the rows §5 names, with the canary-value test as its
   proof.
4. **Fork 4, the predicate: «Неизвестное имя валит строку (Recommended)».** P1: an unknown added `CLAUDE*` name
   fails the row; the compiled non-identity list (`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`,
   `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`) stands, and the obs row that says no such list exists is reworded. He was told a new name
   in a new CLI version then reads that version unverified until he classifies it and a new build ships, and
   that `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_NOTES_DIR` may read red at the first live reading.
5. **Forks 5–7, versions, the cap and «verified»: «2 базовых (второй условно) + 1 запасной (Recommended)».**
   2.1.328 ALONE, re-recorded whole by a live `viola verify --record` in the rig's scratch home; no 2.1.329
   start; no synthetic payload in the recorded set. **TWO base starts and ONE spare, on one ledger:** the first
   (`--cap 1`) is the recording and the first measurement of a hook child's names. **The second (`--cap 2`)
   opens ONLY IF the first read red on the identity row for an unknown name ALONE** — every other row green,
   the cross-session row among them: the names then go to him by the overseer's dialog, he classifies each
   (the floor, or the non-identity list), the code is mended through the revision door, and the second start
   re-records. A red of any other cause — the cross-session row, another row, a scrub refusal — is a finding:
   implement stops and no start follows it. The spare is spent only on a start the rig refuses before its
   ledger line or a host CONTENDED by a neighbour, never on a red reading. From his real home
   `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is READ once per start by the rig; nothing is written under his real
   `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`; no key and no byte into any CLI dialog. «Verified» rests, as shown to him, on the
   live start's step line and stamp, the canary-value test green in CI and the fake agent replaying the
   recorded fixture in CI — for each row its own: v2-26 on the identity row and the `Env` fixture, v2-25 on the
   cross-session row and its recorded payload. A third base start is his.

## Technical answers (the overseer's)

6. **The sender is bounded and inert where it can be:** its own deadline (a closed bound on viola's own child),
   no tool but the send, no session persistence, the print-probe's cwd; a refusal by the model, a missing tool
   or an unknown target reads the row `fail` with a closed word — never a retry inside one verify. Say on the
   P5 card what the sender leaves in the Claude config (a registry entry, a history line), measured or named
   unmeasured, and which residual row carries it.
7. **The misaddressing residual is narrowed in code as far as the bundle allows,** and the plan says how: the
   prompt names ONE session id; if the CLI's send tool takes an exact id rather than a name, use that form; the
   synthetic text is a compiled literal that says what it is (a viola verify probe) so a misaddressed one
   explains itself. Nothing reads the user's other sessions or the registry to «check» — that would be a read
   viola does not own.
8. **The names in the stamp and the fixture are NAMES OF THE CLI'S OWN** after the kept names are removed; the
   canary test also covers a name carrying the user word (the scrub refuses the recording, naming the file and
   its closed code, never the content) and proves the count of non-`CLAUDE` names is a number only.
9. **Order:** both rows' fake-agent cases, the canary test and every control green before the round; an entry

   true by construction WITH its code line.
10. **Every reached row is the wrap's;** a row NOT in your §5 that P4 finds reached is a fork written to
    `founder-forks.md`, not a fold — read the picked rows for what the sender PRINTS, WAITS on and WRITES.
11. **The seam after P5.** When the plan is approved the phase ENDS and nothing else starts. On an account-limit

title: A. The capture arm records env names (27 rows; tests S1–S5; security S2–S5; obs S1, S4)

data.head: ### A. The capture arm records env names (27 rows; tests S1–S5; security S2–S5; obs S1, S4)

body:
1. **`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — `env_capture_document(names)`.** A pure function over an iterator
   of `OsString` names that never sees a value. It returns the bytes of `{"v":1,"claude_names":[…],
   "claude_unshaped":<n>,"other_count":<n>}`:
   - a name whose lossy text starts with `CLAUDE` and is ASCII `[A-Z0-9_]` only goes into `claude_names` (sorted,
     deduplicated);
   - any other `CLAUDE`-prefixed name is counted in `claude_unshaped`. Prefix as `plan_strip` reads it,
     `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:69`;
   - every other name is counted in `other_count`. No other name is written.

   The env-file name helper `env_file_name(k)` = `Env.<k>.json` sits beside `capture_file_name`.
   `parse_capture_file_name` does not parse it: `Env` is no `HookEvent`. So `read_captures`, `free_k` and `ordinal`
   in `src/cmd/hook.rs` skip it unchanged.

2. **`src/cmd/hook.rs` — `capture()`.** After a **SessionStart** payload is filed under its `k`, the arm writes
   `Env.<k>.json` in the same directory:
   - built by step 1 over `std::env::vars_os().map(|(k, _)| k)`, the form `plan_strip`'s caller already uses
     (`src/cmd/verify.rs:192`);
   - written through `create_private_new` + `replace_private` (0600 before any byte).

   It keeps every inertness rule: no `VIOLA_*` read, no obs init, no channel, nothing on stderr, exit 0, nothing
   written on a failure (`(security-plan · decision/hook-capture-arm)`, `(architecture ·
   decision/probe-capture-arms-inert)`). Every other event writes no env file. The doc comment names the env read
   and its ratification (`inputs#I2` item 3). The capture tests in `hook.rs`'s module (1324-1556) that list a
   capture dir after a SessionStart take the env file.

4. **The canary test, new file `tests/security_negatives_env_capture.rs`** (`required-features = ["fake-agent"]`
   in `Cargo.toml`; its binary added to `.config/nextest.toml`'s 20 s override filter beside `cli_verify`, per
   `(test-plan · decision/verify-driven-tests-20s-kill)`). It is modelled on `tests/tui_env_strip.rs`. Its oracle is
   the same literal `STRIPPED` table of canary values: eleven floor names plus `CLAUDE_VIOLA_TEST_NEW_X`. The
   canaries already stand in `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/secret_scan.rs`. Two new canaries,
   `canary-kept-value-<hex4>` and `canary-other-value-<hex4>`, are added to that table
   (`(test-plan · decision/canary-list-single-sourced)`). Phase A cases:
   - `capture_arm_writes_env_names_and_no_value`. It runs `viola hook SessionStart --capture <dir>` with a synthetic
     payload on stdin. The env holds the twelve canary values, plus `ENVCAP_TEST_OTHER=canary-other-value-…` (no
     `VIOLA_` name, `(architecture · decision/viola-env-namespace-product-only)`). Asserted:
     - exit 0, stderr empty;
     - `Env.1.json` is mode 0600;
     - `claude_names` equals the literal sorted twelve, and `other_count` is a JSON number ≥ 1;
     - no canary value's bytes are in any file under `<dir>`;
     - the payload file is byte-equal to stdin.
   - `capture_arm_writes_no_env_file_for_other_events`. A Stop capture leaves no `Env.*` file.

5. **Phase A gates:** entries `cargo fmt --all --check` through `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --e2e` (the first
   seven, §Test Commands). All are green before phase B.

body:
6. **`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — two rows** appended last to `ALL` (`[Self; 29]`). Each reads `pass`
   or `fail` only: `counts` and `row_word` give them no `absent` arm.

   | Variant | Id | Words (fixed ASCII) |
   |---|---|---|
   | `CrossSessionPrefix` (28th) | `cross-session-prefix` | `a message another session sends in opens with a harness prefix` |
   | `IdentityFloor` (29th) | `identity-floor` | `every CLAUDE name the CLI adds to a hook is a known name` |

7. **`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs` — `harness_prefix(prompt) -> Option<&'static str>`.** It returns the
   closed id of the compiled literal the prompt's raw start matches (no trim). The ids are `agent-message`,
   `task-notification`, `cross-session-escaped` and `cross-session`, in `HARNESS_PREFIX_IDS` beside
   `HARNESS_PREFIXES` (hook.rs:135-140).
   - `prompt_origin` (hook.rs:266) is rewritten over it; its result is unchanged.
   - The four literals do not change (`(security-plan · decision/harness-prefix-literals)`).
   - Unit cases: one per literal, and an escaped tag and a leading space give `None`.

8. **`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` — `NON_IDENTITY_HOOK_NAMES: [&str; 3]`** =
   `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, beside `IDENTITY_FLOOR`. It is the founder's P1
   list (`inputs#I2` item 4), as `(security-plan · decision/identity-floor-eleven-names)` names them («the plugin,
   project and env-file names are not identity names»). `IDENTITY_FLOOR` stays eleven names. A test pins the
   literal copy (`(test-plan · decision/identity-floor-tested-against-literal-copy)`).

   Also beside them, the flag literals `ALLOWED_TOOLS_FLAG` = `--allowedTools` and `SEND_TOOL` = `SendMessage` (the
   tool name read statically in the 2.1.328 bundle, `founder-forks.md` T3).

9. **The sender's compiled texts** (`ledger.rs`, beside `PROBE_PROMPT`):
   - `CROSS_SESSION_TEXT` — the message the sender sends. It is synthetic ASCII and says what it is: «viola verify
     probe: a synthetic cross-session message sent by viola verify; reply with the single word ok».
   - `sender_prompt(id)` — `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_HEAD` + `id` + `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_TAIL`. HEAD asks for exactly
     one `SendMessage` call with `to` set to the id that follows. TAIL gives `CROSS_SESSION_TEXT` as the message and
     asks for the single word ok after the call. The id is read only through `is_session_id`.

   One id is named. No registry and no other session is read (`inputs#I2` item 7). The address stays the session id,
   the founder's words (lean T3).

10. **`TypedRun.cross_session: Option<CrossSessionRun>`**, set by step 12: `prompts_before` (Run B's UserPromptSubmit
    count at the sender's spawn), `sender` (`Exited` · `Failed` · `Deadline`), `latency_ms` (from the sender's exit
    to the arrival).

    **`Probes.env: Option<Value>`** is the parsed `Env.<k>.json` of Run B's smallest `k`.

    **`ledger::cross_session_reading(trusted, typed) -> (&'static str, Option<&'static str>)`** — the outcome word
    and the prefix id:
    - `not-run` — no `CrossSessionRun`;
    - `sender-failed` / `sender-deadline` — by `sender`;
    - `no-prompt` — no UserPromptSubmit past `prompts_before` in `trusted`;
    - `unprefixed` — that prompt's `harness_prefix` is `None`;
    - `harness` — otherwise.

    The row passes on `harness` alone. A model refusal, a missing tool and an unknown target all read `no-prompt`:
    viola reads no sender text, so it cannot tell them apart (`inputs#I2` item 6).

    **`ledger::env_reading(env, kept) -> EnvReading { read, added, unknown, other_count, unshaped }`**:
    - `added` = `claude_names` minus every name of `kept` (the config's `claude_env_keep`, read by
      `run::persistent_names` at verify.rs:186), in memory, before anything else reads them;
    - `unknown` = `added` minus `IDENTITY_FLOOR` and `NON_IDENTITY_HOOK_NAMES`.

    The `identity-floor` check passes only when all three hold: `read`, `unknown` empty and `unshaped == 0`
    (`inputs#I2` items 3–4).

11. **`merge_stamp`** (ledger.rs:1300) adds two keys to `measured`:
    - `cross_session_probe` = `{outcome, prefix, latency_ms}`;
    - `env_probe` = `{read, added, unknown, other_count, unshaped}`.

    Names, counts and closed words only (`(architecture · contract/ledger-stamps/content)`). Its signature takes
    the two readings. `record`'s `named_payloads` (verify.rs) adds two files:
    - `Env.recorded-1.json` = `{"v":1,"added":[…]}` from the same reading. Kept names are already gone (`inputs#I2`
      item 8);
    - `UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json`, the arrived prompt's capture, as a framing variant
      (`framing_variants`).

    Both go through `scrubbed_payloads`, and an unclean one refuses the whole recording, naming the file and the
    closed code (`(security-plan · decision/fixture-scrub-and-refusal)`).

12. **Run B's cross-session turn** (`src/cmd/verify/typed/turns.rs` `framing_turns`, `typed/runs.rs`
    `trusted_run`).
    - **Where:** between the `/compact` paste's answer and the `/clear` paste (lean T1). The session id then is
      still `ledger::resume_target`'s (Run B's first SessionStart, `/compact` keeps it), which the same run's agents
      read listed live.
    - **When it runs:** only when the box guard reads the box up and `resume_target` gives an id.
    - **The sender:** spawned through `run_bounded` with subject `verify-sender`, logged as `run_logged` logs:
      - args: `program_args` + `-p <sender_prompt(id)> --model haiku --no-session-persistence --allowedTools
        SendMessage`. No `--plugin-dir`, no `--settings`;
      - cwd: verify's print-probe dir (`Inputs` at `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs:59` gains `sender_cwd`, the
        `ProbeDir`'s `dir`);
      - the same R8 strip;
      - bound: `SENDER_DEADLINE` (120 s, a new const beside `PROBE_DEADLINE` in verify.rs), stopped by the stop.
    - **The wait:** if the sender exited 0, verify waits for one more UserPromptSubmit up to `CROSS_SESSION_WINDOW`
      (30 s, a compiled bound on viola's own wait), then for its turn's end (`added_turn_ended`) up to the probe
      deadline. A non-zero exit or the deadline skips the wait. No retry inside one verify (`inputs#I2` item 6).
    - **After it:** `rows = run.box_wait(now)`. If the guard reads the box up, `/clear` is pasted as today and Run B
      ends by Ctrl-C as today. If it does not, `/clear` is not pasted and Run B ends by `end_by_kill`, no key
      (lean T2, `(architecture · decision/verify-types-nothing-into-dialogs)`). Every other end of Run B is
      unchanged.

14. **The fake agent** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/agents.rs`; tests S3; security S3).
    All fake-agent-only:
    - **Sender:** a `-p` prompt that opens with `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_HEAD` is a sender.
      - It reads the id after the head up to the first space.
      - It finds the registry row beside its executable whose `sessionId` is that id and whose process's parent pid
        (`/proc/<pid>/stat`) equals its own parent pid. Concurrent tests share the exe dir and the recorded id.
      - It writes an empty 0600 `<exe dir>/inbox/<that pid>` and exits 0.
      - With no such row, or a set holding no `UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json`, it exits 1 and writes nothing.
      - It fires no hook.
    - **Receiver:** under `--framing`, an interactive fake polls `<exe dir>/inbox/<own pid>` on `CONTROL_POLL`. On
      it, the fake removes the file, fires `UserPromptSubmit` variant `cross-session-1` as recorded, then
      `end_turn(None)`.
    - **`--cross-session-turn-screen <phase>`:** a new option, parsed beside `--tag-turn-screen`, for step 18's
      kill case alone.
    - **Env replay:** when the set holds `Env.recorded-1.json`, every SessionStart hook child is spawned with each
      `added` name set to the compiled placeholder `FAKE_AGENT_ENV_VALUE` (`fake-agent`). That is how the capture
      arm reads the recorded names over the fake. The fake's own receipts are unchanged
      (`(test-plan · contract/fake-agent-receipt/env)`).
    - **Cases** in `test_cases_modes.rs`:
      - `sender_delivers_only_to_its_siblings_session` — the sender reaches the row of its parent's child alone, and
        exits 1 with no inbox file for another parent's row;
      - `receiver_fires_the_cross_session_variant_once`;
      - `session_start_hook_carries_the_recorded_env_names`.

15. **The test-built synthetic sets** (`tests/support/verify.rs`; committed nowhere, written at test run time like
    `dialog_set`, the precedent `chunks/2026-11-20-permissionrequest-question-answered` step 13b):
    - `framing_set()` gains `UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1`, a prompt opening `<cross-session-message from=`;
    - a new `write_env_set(fixtures, version, names)` writes `Env.recorded-1.json`.

    Each is named SYNTHETIC in its doc comment and a one-line comment above it. The default names are three floor
    names and `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`.

16. **Unit cases** (ledger test files; rstest tables per tests S2):
    - **`test_cases_checks.rs`:**
      - `cross_session_prefix_passes_on_a_prefixed_arrival`.
      - `cross_session_prefix_fails_when`, in this case order: `case_1_not_run`, `case_2_no_prefix` (`unprefixed`),
        `case_3_no_prompt`, `case_4_sender_failed`, `case_5_sender_deadline`.
      - `identity_floor_passes_on_floor_and_hook_names`.
      - `identity_floor_fails_when`, in this case order: `case_1_unread`, `case_2_unknown_name`,
        `case_3_unshaped_name`.
      - `identity_floor_drops_kept_names_before_the_check`: a kept unknown name passes and is absent from `added`.
    - **`test_cases_stamps.rs`:** `merge_stamp` writes both measured blocks, names and counts only. A 27-row stamp
      reads unverified, and a 29-row one verified. Every relied-count literal moves.
    - **`test_cases.rs`:** the row-count and verdict vectors at 29.
    - **`test_cases_runs.rs`:** `framing_variants` names `cross-session-1`.
    - Every count is swept by `len()` and by the summaries' sums (testing.md 2026-11-19).

20. **The rig (test-only, `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`).**
    - **Labels:** `Arm::of_label` maps `HF`, `HF-2` and `HG` to `Arm::VR`.
    - **Kept stamps:** `StampShape::of` gives `HF` and `HF-2` `Keep(FLOOR_STAMP)` (`floor-stamp.json`), and `HG`
      `Keep(FLOOR_STAMP_2)` (`floor-stamp-2.json`). F-P4-1 (a).
    - **Summary lines:** `stamp_lines` (mod.rs:2809) prints four new lines, `unread` when there is no entry:
      - `cross-session-prefix: <word>`;
      - `identity-floor: <word>`;
      - `cross-session: <measured.cross_session_probe.outcome>`, a code word or `unread`;
      - `env-unknown: <count of measured.env_probe.unknown>`.
    - **`FLOOR_ROWS`:** takes both rows, 23 → 25, its rule «every relied row but four» kept
      (`the_floor_rows_are_every_relied_row_but_four`).
    - The doc comments name the labels. The label and stamp-shape tables (mod.rs:3245, :3409) and the `stamp_lines`
      cases take the new rows.

21. **Phase B gates:** entries 8–14 (§Test Commands), then the controls `kept-names-removed`, `floor-unknown-fails`
    and `prefix-match`. All are green and «holds» before the round. The stamped-home suites are not run here (above).

title: C. The live start `S1` (`HF`): two base starts, one conditional, and one spare (`inputs#I2` item 5)

data.head: ### C. The live start `S1` (`HF`): two base starts, one conditional, and one spare (`inputs#I2` item 5)

body:
22. **Read the host first:** `python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py
    read --last 15`, by hand. The verdict line goes to `evidence/live-round.md`.
    - A CONTENDED reading that names a NEIGHBOUR stops: re-read later, never retried into (`inputs#I1` item 7).
    - This repository's own gate stall is no neighbour (verification-harness.md 2026-11-19).

23. **The round** (`gate.py run --chunk 2026-11-20-harness-prefix-and-identity-floor-ledger-rows --run-dir {implement
    run dir} --live-legs`, or entry by entry with `--entry {n}`) fires these in block order, each right before
    `S1`:
    1. the install read by path;
    2. the census;
    3. the plain build with its hashes (verification-harness.md 2026-10-20);
    4. the kept record and stamp read absent;
    5. the live home's stamp sha recorded once;
    6. the runtime dir read owner-only;
    7. `S1` under `--cap 1 --spare 1`.

    **Disk state outside the tree** (`inputs#I1` item 4, `inputs#I2` item 9). Each is either an entry or true by
    construction, with its code line:
    - The kept record `target/live-rig/HF/record/` and the kept stamp `target/live-rig/floor-stamp.json`: ABSENT,
      read by an entry (4).
    - The live home's stamps sha: recorded before (entry 5) and read unmoved after.
    - `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` owner-only: an entry (6). The VR arm keeps the variable in its child's env
      (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs:24-32`). The CLI's cross-session socket lives under it
      (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cc-socks/`, `founder-forks.md` §2), now for two sessions.
    - The install by path and the build hash: entries (1, 3).
    - The census: an entry (2), and again keyed `operator` after the last live leg (`inputs#I1` item 5).
    - A standing rig scratch home: true BY CONSTRUCTION. Each start makes `<scratch base>/<run>` from the rig's own pid
      and start time (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/procs.rs:64-68`, `mod.rs:552-555`) on tmpfs.
    - A standing `.viola-verify-*` dir: true BY CONSTRUCTION. Verify's cwd is the fresh scratch's own `cwd`
      (`mod.rs:1182`), and `TrustedDir::create` removes a standing one (`src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs:301-304`).

    A start refused for the token window (before its ledger line) is uncounted: implement stops, says so, and sets no
    timer (`inputs#I1` items 7, 10).

25. **A red `S1`.** The founder's rule (`inputs#I2` item 5), applied to the rig summary's own words.
    - **First:** implement records the rig summary whole in `evidence/live-round.md`, closed words only. It fires the
      kept-stamp and env-names after-reads by `--entry`, and they read even on a red.
    - **The one red that opens a second base start:** `identity-floor: fail` with `env-unknown` ≥ 1, `failing:
      identity-floor` alone, every other row `pass` (`cross-session-prefix: pass` among them), and the record not
      refused.
      - Implement stops and hands the `unknown` names (names only) to the overseer for the founder's dialog.
      - He classifies each, onto the floor or onto `NON_IDENTITY_HOOK_NAMES`.
      - The code is mended through the phase's revision door.
      - That revision's round fires `HG` under `--cap 2 --spare 1`, which re-records.
    - **Any other red is a finding:** the cross-session row, another row, a scrub refusal, `env-unknown` 0 with
      `identity-floor: fail` (an unread or unshaped capture). Implement stops and no start follows it.
    - **The spare `HF-2`:** only for a start the rig refuses before its ledger line, or a host read CONTENDED by a
      neighbour. Never for a red reading. A third base start is the founder's.

26. **No key and no byte into any CLI dialog.**
    - The rig types none.
    - Verify types only its compiled pastes, and every probe dialog is answered by the capture hook's closed ids.
    - The sender raises none: print mode, one allowed tool.
    - From the real home, `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is READ once per start by the rig: a 0600 copy, removed on
      every exit path.
    - Nothing is written under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola` (`inputs#I2` item 5;
      `(security-plan · decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty)`).

27. **Copy `target/live-rig/HF/record/2.1.328/` over `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/`.** Every recorded file replaces its
    namesake, the two new files join, and `Mcp.tools-list-1.json` stays as committed.
    - A plain copy, never edited or re-serialised.
    - `evidence/landing.md` lists the files with sha256 prefixes, and the identity read (testing.md 2026-10-14), before
      anything runs over the set.
    - A file the hygiene suite refuses is a red, never scrubbed.

28. **`tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`** walks `Env.recorded-1.json` (the env class: `v` 1 and `added`, an array
    of names matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`) and the `cross-session` framing stem.

29. **`tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs`.** Its two verify-exit assertions (the precedent's step 25a) expect exit 0
    only on a set holding both `question-permission` and `cross-session` variants. On every other framed set they
    expect exit 1, AND exactly the step lines of the rows that set lacks read `fail`: `permission-request-question`
    and/or `cross-session-prefix`. The summary's fail count equals that number. The byte drift is still compared on
    every set.

32. Operator entries, after implement's report: pre-push, the hygiene read, then `rec.py land` and the pre-CI commit,
    then the push, then the CI read.
- `tests/security_negatives_env_capture.rs` — the canary-value test: the capture arm's names-only env file, kept names removed before stamp and record, the user-word name
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/Env.recorded-1.json` — `S1`'s recorded env names, through the scrub
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json` — `S1`'s recorded cross-session arrival

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — two rows, `env_capture_document`, `env_file_name`, the sender texts, `cross_session_reading`, `env_reading`, the measured blocks, `Probes.env`, `TypedRun.cross_session`, `framing_variants`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases.rs` — row-count and verdict vectors at 29
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_checks.rs` — the two rows' pass and fail tables
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_stamps.rs` — measured blocks, 27-row unverified, relied counts
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_runs.rs` — the `cross-session-1` framing variant
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` — `NON_IDENTITY_HOOK_NAMES`, `ALLOWED_TOOLS_FLAG`, `SEND_TOOL`, the literal-copy case
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs` — `harness_prefix`, `HARNESS_PREFIX_IDS`, `prompt_origin` over it, cases
- `src/cmd/hook.rs` — the capture arm's SessionStart env file, its doc comment, the capture cases
- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — `SENDER_DEADLINE`, `sender_cwd`, the env file read, `env_reading`, 29 step lines, the record's two files, the scrub unit case
- `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs` — Run B's end by kill when the box is not up after the cross-session turn
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — `Inputs` (typed.rs:59) gains `sender_cwd`
- `src/cmd/verify/typed/turns.rs` — the cross-session turn between `/compact` and `/clear`, the sender spawn and its waits
- `src/run/version_gate.rs` — test module only: `stamps_verdict_needs_the_dialog_rows` at 29
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — `verify-sender` in the subject enum
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — the fake sender, the inbox receiver, the Env replay on SessionStart hooks
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/agents.rs` — the registry lookup by session id and parent pid, the inbox path
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/test_cases_modes.rs` — the three fake cases
- `tests/support/verify.rs` — the synthetic `cross-session-1` framing shape and `write_env_set`, named synthetic
- `tests/cli_verify.rs` — the five rows' fake cases, relied counts, process-line lists
- `tests/cli_verify/runs.rs` — relied and summary literals
- `tests/cli_verify/stamps.rs` — relied and summary literals
- `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs` — `ROW_IDS` 29, the summary literal
- `tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs` — the verify-exit assertions keyed on the variants a set holds
- `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` — the env class and the `cross-session` stem
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — `LIVE_PASS` and relied literals
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/secret_scan.rs` — the two new canaries in the table
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — `HF` / `HF-2` / `HG`, `FLOOR_STAMP`, `FLOOR_STAMP_2`, four summary lines, `FLOOR_ROWS`, cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — relied literals
- `Cargo.toml` — the new test's `[[test]]` with `required-features = ["fake-agent"]`
- `.config/nextest.toml` — the new binary on the 20 s override
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/` — re-recorded whole by `S1`; `Mcp.tools-list-1.json` kept
The block runs in this order:

- **Phase A** (the capture arm, 27 rows): the formatter, the linter, the root bin's unit cases, the canary test, then
  the workspace unit, integration and E2E layers.

- **Phase B** (the rows): the formatter, the linter, the agent crate's cases (the `floor-unknown-fails` and
  `prefix-match` controls' entry), the rig's library cases, the root bin's unit cases, the rows' `cli_verify` cases
  and the canary test (the `kept-names-removed` control's entry).

- **The round:** the install read, the census, the plain build with its hash, the kept record and stamp absence, the
  live home's stamp sha, the runtime dir owner-only. Then `S1`, then the census keyed `operator`.

- **The after-reads:** the kept stamp at 29, the env names (report-only), the live home's sha unmoved, and the
  record's names against the committed set.
- **After the landing:** the `diff -r`, then the unit, integration and E2E layers, then the boot smoke.
- **The operator pass.**
What is not run, and why:
- No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 8). obs S5's mutation clause is not exercised.

- No release check entry: CI's `release` job runs `scripts/release-check.sh` on the push. The fake agent stays
  behind `fake-agent`.
- Between phase B and the landing, no stamped-home suite runs (§Steps intro).
Bounds and homes:
- Every test start runs under its test-owned home and user home (tests S3, arch S1).
- Every test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint: the new binary sits on the 20 s override.

- The live start runs under the rig's private scratch at `/tmp/viola-rig-<uid>/`. The rig's `--deadline` bounds
  `S1` under the entry's `timeout`.

The live leg's non-priming probes are the round entries ahead of it; none primes anything. `S1` is ledgered in
`.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-20-harness-prefix-and-identity-floor-ledger-rows/evidence/floor-starts.ndjson`.
`--cap` is the running total of base lines in that one file (`inputs#I1` item 5).

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries (validation.md
check 4 (6)).
- Each reads «holds» only when its case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line.
- Each fires on a whole-binary entry, so the control record lists by name every case that failed in the removed run.
- «holds» needs the guard's OWN case among them.

The values guard has no control: the arm never reads a value (step 2's `vars_os().map(|(k, _)| k)`), so no deletion
can make it keep one. The canary test is its proof.
| | `kept-names-removed` | `floor-unknown-fails` | `prefix-match` |
| **File** | `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` | `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` | `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` |

| **The edit removes** | the clause of `env_reading` that removes `kept` from `added` | the clause of the `identity-floor` check that requires `unknown` empty | the clause of `cross_session_reading` that reads `unprefixed` when `harness_prefix` is `None` |
| **Case** | `kept_name_reaches_no_stamp_or_record` | `identity_floor_fails_when::case_2_unknown_name` | `cross_session_prefix_fails_when::case_2_no_prefix` |

| **Fired on** | `cargo nextest run -p viola --features fake-agent --test security_negatives_env_capture --no-fail-fast`, `--timeout 600` | `cargo nextest run -p viola-agent-claude --no-fail-fast`, `--timeout 600` | the same, `--timeout 600` |
Implement quotes each edit's exact text in its control record.

body:
- (cross-session) `matrix#v2-25`: the prefix the CLI puts on a message another session sends in is the stamped
  relied row `cross-session-prefix`.
  - Its probe is a print-mode sender's one `SendMessage` into Run B. It passes only when the arrival's raw start is
    a compiled harness literal: outcome `harness`.
  - Live on 2.1.328 in `S1`: `cross-session-prefix: pass`, `cross-session: harness`, `pass-count: 29/29`, and the
    kept stamp at `29 ok`.
  - Over the fake agent:
    - `cross_session_prefix_reads_pass_over_the_fake_sender` in the phase B `cli_verify` entry;
    - after the landing, `contract_ledger_probes` replays the recorded `UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json`, with
      2.1.328 at `29 pass 0 fail`, in the `run --e2e` entry.
  - (`(architecture · decision/harness-prompt-prefixes)`, `(security-plan · decision/harness-prefix-literals)`.)

- (identity) `matrix#v2-26`: the `CLAUDE*` names the CLI adds to a hook child are the stamped relied row
  `identity-floor`. Its probe reads names only.
  - Live on 2.1.328 in `S1`: `identity-floor: pass`, `env-unknown: 0`, and the kept stamp's `env_probe.added`
    copied into the evidence.
  - No value reaches any capture, log, stamp or fixture: the canary test (`security_negatives_env_capture`) is
    green in the phase A and B entries and in CI.
  - After the landing, the fake agent replays the recorded `Env.recorded-1.json` in `contract_ledger_probes`.
  - (`(architecture · decision/r8-identity-floor)`, `(test-plan · decision/env-names-only)`.)

- (rows) Each new row's pass case and its fail table are green. The `floor-unknown-fails` and `prefix-match`
  controls read «holds». A 27-row stamp reads unverified and a 29-row one verified (step 16).

- (capture) The capture arm writes `Env.<k>.json` on SessionStart alone: names only, 0600, no value. Kept names are
  gone before the stamp and the record. The `kept-names-removed` control reads «holds». A name carrying the user word
  records nothing, and the scrub refuses it by file and `username` (step 19).

- (Run B) After the cross-session turn, Run B ends by a kill with no key when the box is not up
  (`cross_session_prefix_ends_run_b_by_kill_when_the_box_is_not_up`).

- (counts) Every relied-count literal reads 29, and the verify step lines read `[NN/29]`: the phase B unit entries
  and the after-landing layers.

- (live) `S1` reads green on its entry's atoms within the founder's cap: `HF` is base line 1, and `HG` and `HF-2`
  are unspent unless step 25 opens them.
  - The after-reads hold: the kept stamp at `29 ok`, `live-stamp: unmoved`, and the name diff at exactly 3 lines.
  - Before the start, the round's runtime-dir entry reads `runtime-dir: owner-only`.
  - A red `S1` is recorded as read and verifies nothing
    (`(test-plan · decision/live-failing-reading-not-verification)`).

- (fixtures) `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/` is the record copied whole: the `diff -r` entry prints nothing. The set passes
  hygiene and drift in the after-landing `run --e2e` entry (`(test-plan · decision/hook-payloads-recorded-by-verify)`).

- (tests) The whole unit, integration and E2E layers return `"ok":true` after the landing. The pre-push gate and CI
  read green.

- Rows (the union and standing lists of the take-up run, read by search: their sum, 328 850 B, is past 250 000 B):
  - architecture: `decision/capability-ledger` · `decision/harness-prompt-prefixes` ·
    `decision/harness-prompts-not-human` · `decision/r8-identity-floor` · `decision/identity-floor-eleven-names` ·
    `decision/verify-child-set` · `decision/verify-types-nothing-into-dialogs` · `decision/probe-capture-arms-inert`
    · `decision/verify-run-e-resumes-run-b-first-session` · `decision/verify-box-wait-for-literal` ·
    `decision/unverified-cli-transport-only` · `decision/viola-env-namespace-product-only` ·
    `contract/ledger-stamps/content` · `contract/hook-capture-arm/payload-file` ·
    `contract/config-json/claude-env-keep`;
  - security-plan: `decision/verify-children-direct-spawn` · `decision/verify-never-answers-dialogs` ·
    `decision/verify-writes-no-dialog-byte` · `decision/hook-capture-arm` · `decision/capture-arms-isolated` ·
    `decision/harness-prefix-literals` · `decision/identity-floor-eleven-names` · `decision/r8-claude-env-strip` ·
    `decision/new-env-read-needs-log-entry` · `decision/no-messaging-secrets-in-outputs` ·
    `decision/verify-probe-captures-transient` · `decision/live-rig-kept-stamp-owner-only` ·
    `decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty` · `decision/compiled-classification-sources`;
  - test-plan: `decision/ledger-row-verify-probe` · `decision/identity-floor-tested-against-literal-copy` ·
    `decision/canary-list-single-sourced` · `decision/synthetic-inputs-with-canary` ·
    `decision/verify-driven-tests-20s-kill` · `decision/tests-never-read-host-sessions` ·
    `decision/record-only-at-zero-failing-rows` · `decision/hook-payloads-recorded-by-verify` ·
    `decision/fake-agent-matches-verify-fixtures` · `decision/live-failing-reading-not-verification` ·
    `decision/standing-live-rig` · `contract/fake-agent-receipt/env`;
  - obs-plan: `decision/identity-floor-always-stripped` · `decision/env-names-only` ·
    `decision/hook-capture-arms-unlogged` · `contract/verify-spawn-subject/agents-probe` ·
    `contract/diag-subject/agents-probe` · `contract/child-spawn-log/subject`;
  - a11y-plan: `decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` · `decision/time-bounds-never-on-human`;
  - design-system: `contract/viola-verify-output/summary-line`;
  - layout-templates: `contract/viola-verify/summary`.
- Every row cited above was found in its master's rows file of the take-up run (the P4 searches).

- Standing lines: tests S1–S7, arch S1–S5, security S1–S5, obs S1–S4 (S5 not exercised: no mutation run), design
  S1–S2, layouts S1, a11y S1–S5.

- **Path (B), verify reading the CLI's published auth key; path (C), a token of verify's own in Run B's env.** Both
  were declined: verify reads no CLI credential and sets no floor name (`inputs#I2` item 2).
- **E2, a new hidden arm or probe child for the names** — declined (`inputs#I2` item 3).
- **P2, a row that never fails; P3, every added name of any prefix** — declined (`inputs#I2` item 4).

- **Recording or stamping 2.1.329; a synthetic payload inside the recorded set** — declined (`inputs#I2` item 5). The
  test-built synthetic sets of steps 15 and 18 are committed nowhere and are named synthetic, as in the precedent's
  step 13b.

- **Reading the user's other sessions or the registry to «check» the target** — a read viola does not own
  (`inputs#I2` item 7).
- **A retry of the sender inside one verify** (`inputs#I2` item 6).
- **Widening the four harness literals to more of the CLI's sixteen tags** — no part of this entry.

- **Adding a name to `IDENTITY_FLOOR` or `NON_IDENTITY_HOOK_NAMES` without the founder's classification** — that is
  step 25's revision, on his word only.
- **Ctrl-C into Run B after a cross-session turn whose box is not up** — a key into a possible dialog (lean T2).

- **Any key or byte into a CLI dialog; a second base start outside step 25's one red; spending `HF-2` on a red**
  (`inputs#I2` item 5).

- **Any read of the real `~/.claude*`** beyond the rig's one credentials read and its read-only stamp of
  `~/.claude.json`. Any write under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`. Any read of `~/.viola` but the stamp's sha.

- **An atom on `browser-tools-prompt`, on the env names, or on any word that can honestly read two ways** — each is a
  READING (`inputs#I1` item 6).

- **A value of any environment variable read, kept or logged** — the arm reads names alone
  (`(security-plan · decision/no-messaging-secrets-in-outputs)`).
- **A figure in a documentation leaf** (`inputs#I1` Facts).
- **A scheduled wake or timer, with any argument** (`inputs#I1` item 10).

- **HOLD on F-P4-1 and F-P4-2** (Metadata). Option (a) of each is planned. F-P4-1 (b) would re-label `S1` as `PQ`
  and add a move-aside entry. F-P4-2 (b) would give `cross-session-prefix` an `absent` arm. Either returns the plan
  to P4.

- **The leans T1–T5** (`founder-forks.md`) are the overseer's to strike. No founder ruling moves with them.
  - T1 places the send between `/compact` and `/clear`. Then the id is still the one `resume_target` reads, which the
    P3 block's §2 named, and §2's «after its framing pastes» holds for every paste but `/clear`.
  - T2 ends Run B by a kill only when the box is not up after that turn.

- **The sender's static facts, read from the 2.1.328 bundle with no start.**
  - The tool is `SendMessage`, input `to` and `message`. `to` takes a `uds:` socket path, a bare `/…/*.sock` path,
    `bridge:` or `did:`; anything else falls to an `other` scheme.
  - The tool is marked deferred.
  - Delivery follows the receiver's `crossSessionInbound` setting: unset means permission-mode parity; a value can
    turn messages away or hold them for approval.
  - Each of these is a premise only `S1` measures. A red from one is a finding (step 25).

- **What the sender leaves in the Claude config** (`inputs#I2` item 6):
  - no transcript (`--no-session-persistence`);
  - no new project dir: it runs in the print probe's cwd, whose project dir verify's print probe already leaves;
  - unmeasured: a session-registry entry, an input-history line, and a socket under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cc-socks/`
    while it runs.

  The rows that carry it are `(security-plan · decision/verify-real-cli-transcripts-accepted)`, its architecture
  twin and the new misaddressing residual row (Expected amendments).

- **Carry `cry-ttj3ml2l`** (WATCH, the CI-only `cli_wheel path5_a_turn_left_running_is_cleared_by_pause_then_release`
  red). It is read at each run from the test's own line. Its third green, ci#44789020820 on `b3eb184c`, stands in the
  scope, and its retirement rule reads «a recurrence, or 3 green runs». Retiring it is the wrap's route adaptation. At
  a red, the job log and the test's own events are read before any mend, and a CI red on it is not re-run before the
  overseer's word (`inputs#I1` item 1).

- **Carry `cry-sutjgyh6`** (the intermittent `rig_rehearsal_reads_the_box_empty_after_x_and_del` red). It is acted on
  only at its next red: the printed rig summary and the kept `after-del` frame are read and the cause named before
  the wait is mended. No retry, no loosened entry. The after-landing `run --e2e` entry runs the rehearsals.

- **Widenings, each the founder's own answer to the fork that showed it** (`inputs#I2` items 2–3), so rule
  `rul-bznresq5` applies and the wrap halts once, as an answer card:
  - W1: verify's child set gains the print-mode sender, and Run B one cross-session turn;
  - W2: the capture arm reads its process's env names and writes one more file;
  - W3: the misaddressing residual.

  F-P4-1 and F-P4-2 join that card only on his own answer. None of the four `verdict: escalate` patterns names
  anything else here.

- **Expected amendments (wrap)** — W1–W3 under `rul-bznresq5` (`inputs#I2` items 2–4). F-P4-1 and F-P4-2 follow his
  answer. No row states a count (`inputs#I1` Facts).
  - architecture §Established Decisions — `(architecture · decision/verify-child-set)` gains the print-mode sender
    and Run B's cross-session turn (W1). `(architecture · decision/probe-capture-arms-inert)` keeps every inert rule,
    and the SessionStart capture also writes its env-names file (W2).
  - architecture §Standard Contracts — `(architecture · contract/hook-capture-arm/payload-file)` gains the
    `Env.<k>.json` file. `(architecture · contract/ledger-stamps/content)` gains the `cross_session_probe` and
    `env_probe` measured blocks: closed words, names, counts.
  - security-plan — `(security-plan · decision/verify-children-direct-spawn)` gains the sender, a direct non-PTY
    spawn under the R8 strip (W1).
  - security-plan — `(security-plan · decision/hook-capture-arm)` and `(security-plan · decision/capture-arms-isolated)`
    gain the env-names read (W2). A Decisions Log entry records it, owed by
    `(security-plan · decision/new-env-read-needs-log-entry)`.
  - security-plan — a new residual row beside `(security-plan · decision/verify-echo-probe-residuals)`: the
    misaddressing residual in a real config, under the automatic verify too (W3). With F-P4-2 (a), it also names the
    `crossSessionInbound` residual.
  - security-plan — `(security-plan · decision/verify-real-cli-transcripts-accepted)` and
    `(security-plan · decision/verify-trusted-runs-risk)`, and architecture
    `(architecture · decision/verify-transcripts-accepted-residual)`, name the sender's unmeasured registry entry,
    history line and socket.
  - security-plan — `(security-plan · decision/live-rig-kept-stamp-owner-only)` gains `HF` and `HG` (F-P4-1 (a)).
  - security-plan / test-plan — `(security-plan · decision/r8-claude-env-strip)` and
    `(test-plan · decision/env-names-only)`: the probe also reads names only.
    `(security-plan · decision/fixture-scrub-and-refusal)`, `decision/recorder-scrub` and
    `decision/verify-probe-captures-transient` gain the env fixture class.
  - test-plan — `(test-plan · decision/hook-payloads-recorded-by-verify)`,
    `(test-plan · decision/fake-agent-matches-verify-fixtures)`, `decision/fake-agent-replay-for-stamps` and
    `decision/one-verify-stamp-per-build` gain the env fixture and the cross-session variant.
    `(test-plan · decision/standing-live-rig)` gains the `HF` and `HG` labels.
  - obs-plan — `(obs-plan · decision/identity-floor-always-stripped)` is reworded per P1 (`inputs#I2` item 4): the
    eleven names are always removed, and beyond them a compiled list of three non-identity hook names exists only for
    the verify probe's classification. New rows `contract/verify-spawn-subject/verify-sender` and
    `contract/diag-subject/verify-sender`; `contract/process-log/child-and-probe-lifecycle` names the sender.
  - a11y-plan — `(a11y-plan · decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver)` holds («viola's own child»).
    `decision/human-keystrokes-never-blocked`' except holds: the automatic verify's window lengthens, and no word
    moves. No amendment.
  - matrix — none beyond the claims.

# One technical question before the founder sees F-P4-1 and F-P4-2 — «Harness-prefix and identity-floor ledger rows»

This relay, `relay-harness-p3.md` and the phase directive are the only files of this folder you read or snap.
Answer from the tree and the installed bundles as strings, with NO start, by APPENDING a short section «Answer to
the overseer's P5 question» to your `founder-forks.md`; if the answer adds an option to F-P4-2, add it there with
its cost. Change no plan line. Then stop again at the card. Start nothing.

**F-P4-2 has no option in which verify's OWN child accepts the message whatever the user's setting says.** Run C
already carries a compiled `--settings` literal (`DIALOG_SETTINGS`) so that its dialogs are raised whatever the
user's settings hold. Say, by reading the 2.1.328 and 2.1.329 bundles:
1. the closed set of values `crossSessionInbound` takes and what each does; whether one of them ACCEPTS an inbound
   cross-session message from any local sender without holding it;
2. where the CLI reads that setting from — whether a `--settings` argument on Run B's own command line can set it
   for that one session (as `DIALOG_SETTINGS` does for Run C's rule), and whether a user, project or managed
   settings file would override or be overridden by it (the bundle's precedence, as far as strings show it);
3. whether the «permission-mode class» match between sender and receiver is also settable for the pair verify
   spawns (both are verify's children: say what class each runs in under the plan as written, and whether the
   sender's `-p` mode puts it in another class than Run B's interactive one — if so the message is HELD on this
   very host and `S1` reads red by construction);
4. if such a compiled setting exists: it is a third option of F-P4-2 — «Run B carries a compiled `--settings`
   that accepts inbound cross-session messages for that one verify child» — price it: what it widens (a verify
   child accepting messages from any local session for its seconds of life, inside a 0700 probe dir, under the
   R8 strip), which rows it reaches, what stays unmeasured, and whether the row can still FAIL on a CLI that
   changed delivery (it should).
Point 3 matters most: if the plan as written holds the message on this host, say so plainly.

- **Authority:**
  - The founder's own answers, relayed verbatim by the overseer: items 1–5 of `inputs#I2`, and F-P4-1 (a) and

- **Revision at P5 (rev 5, `inputs#I3`):** F-P4-2 (c) is folded into steps 9, 12, 14 and 18, the touchpoints and the
  Expected amendments. T3's lookup miss and T5's leavings are written as plan text. Nothing else moves: the cap, both
  predicates, the version and what «verified» rests on (`inputs#I3` item 4).

9. **The sender's compiled texts** (`ledger.rs`, beside `PROBE_PROMPT`):
   - `CROSS_SESSION_TEXT` — the message the sender sends. It is synthetic ASCII and says what it is: «viola verify
     probe: a synthetic cross-session message sent by viola verify; reply with the single word ok».
   - `sender_prompt(id)` — `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_HEAD` + `id` + `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_TAIL`. HEAD asks for exactly
     one `SendMessage` call with `to` set to the id that follows. TAIL gives `CROSS_SESSION_TEXT` as the message and
     asks for the single word ok after the call. The id is read only through `is_session_id`.

   - `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS` = `{"crossSessionInbound":"accept"}` — Run B's compiled `--settings` literal, beside
     `DIALOG_SETTINGS` (ledger.rs:314). It is the founder's F-P4-2 (c) (`inputs#I3`), and it is the only settings
     document Run B carries.

   One id is named. No registry and no other session is read (`inputs#I2` item 7). The address stays the session id,
   the founder's words (lean T3, standing per `inputs#I3` item 2). **A lookup miss is a finding:** a session id the
   CLI's send tool cannot resolve sends nothing, so the row reads `no-prompt`. Implement stops (step 25), and no
   mechanism is added for it.

12. **Run B's cross-session turn** (`src/cmd/verify/typed/turns.rs` `framing_turns`, `typed/runs.rs`
    `trusted_run`).
    - **Where:** between the `/compact` paste's answer and the `/clear` paste (lean T1). The session id then is
      still `ledger::resume_target`'s (Run B's first SessionStart, `/compact` keeps it), which the same run's agents
      read listed live.
    - **Run B's args** (`trusted_args`, `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs`): the run's own args, then `SETTINGS_FLAG`
      and `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS`, then the plugin dir (F-P4-2 (c), `inputs#I3`). That is the same form
      `dialog_run` uses for `DIALOG_SETTINGS`.
      - It overrides the user's own `crossSessionInbound` and default-mode parity for Run B alone.
      - Managed policy, a repo or local setting that tightens, an invalid value and the CLI's `receive` switch still
        win, and each reads the row `fail` (`founder-forks.md`, «Answer to the overseer's P5 question»).
      - The sender carries no settings.
    - **When it runs:** only when the box guard reads the box up and `resume_target` gives an id.
    - **The sender:** spawned through `run_bounded` with subject `verify-sender`, logged as `run_logged` logs:
      - args: `program_args` + `-p <sender_prompt(id)> --model haiku --no-session-persistence --allowedTools
        SendMessage`. No `--plugin-dir`, no `--settings`;
      - cwd: verify's print-probe dir (`Inputs` at `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs:59` gains `sender_cwd`, the
        `ProbeDir`'s `dir`);
      - the same R8 strip;
      - bound: `SENDER_DEADLINE` (120 s, a new const beside `PROBE_DEADLINE` in verify.rs), stopped by the stop.
    - **The wait:** if the sender exited 0, verify waits for one more UserPromptSubmit up to `CROSS_SESSION_WINDOW`
      (30 s, a compiled bound on viola's own wait), then for its turn's end (`added_turn_ended`) up to the probe
      deadline. A non-zero exit or the deadline skips the wait. No retry inside one verify (`inputs#I2` item 6).
    - **After it:** `rows = run.box_wait(now)`. If the guard reads the box up, `/clear` is pasted as today and Run B
      ends by Ctrl-C as today. If it does not, `/clear` is not pasted and Run B ends by `end_by_kill`, no key
      (lean T2, `(architecture · decision/verify-types-nothing-into-dialogs)`). Every other end of Run B is
      unchanged.

14. **The fake agent** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/agents.rs`; tests S3; security S3).
    All fake-agent-only:
    - **Sender:** a `-p` prompt that opens with `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_HEAD` is a sender.
      - It reads the id after the head up to the first space.
      - It finds the registry row beside its executable whose `sessionId` is that id and whose process's parent pid
        (`/proc/<pid>/stat`) equals its own parent pid. Concurrent tests share the exe dir and the recorded id.
      - It writes an empty 0600 `<exe dir>/inbox/<that pid>` and exits 0.
      - With no such row, or a set holding no `UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json`, it exits 1 and writes nothing.
      - It fires no hook.
    - **Receiver:** under `--framing`, an interactive fake polls `<exe dir>/inbox/<own pid>` on `CONTROL_POLL`, but

      the flag as the CLI would read the setting. On the inbox file, the fake removes it, fires `UserPromptSubmit`
      variant `cross-session-1` as recorded, then `end_turn(None)`. Without the literal it reads no inbox.
    - **`--cross-session-turn-screen <phase>`:** a new option, parsed beside `--tag-turn-screen`, for step 18's

    - **Env replay:** when the set holds `Env.recorded-1.json`, every SessionStart hook child is spawned with each

    - **Cases** in `test_cases_modes.rs`:

      - `receiver_fires_the_cross_session_variant_once`;

        another document, fires nothing and stays in place;

18. **The rows' fake-agent cases** (`tests/cli_verify.rs`, over a synthetic set at a test-owned version, tests S3).
    The fake agent is planted by the shared helpers alone (`(test-plan · decision/tests-never-read-host-sessions)`).
    - `cross_session_prefix_reads_pass_over_the_fake_sender`:
      - step line `[28/29] cross-session-prefix … pass`;
      - the stamp's `cross_session_probe` reads `{"outcome":"harness","prefix":"cross-session",…}`;

    - **The keep-the-red case** (`inputs#I3` item 1), ONE rstest:

# Implement directive — «Harness-prefix and identity-floor ledger rows» (chunk 2026-11-20-harness-prefix-and-identity-floor-ledger-rows)

The plan is approved (P5 card 1). This window is fresh: read the chunk's documents and run dir from disk first. This
directive is the only file of its folder you read or snap.

**In your own chat messages never print a compiled screen literal verbatim**: name it. This session is driven
through the pinned product, which holds none of the last four mends: call no scheduled-wake or timer tool.

## The live cap for THIS chunk (the founder's own answers, 2026-11-21; nothing widens it)

- **TWO base starts and ONE spare, on one ledger (`evidence/floor-starts.ndjson`), claude 2.1.328 by path, under the
  rig's PRIVATE config and scratch home.** The first, `S1` under the rig label `HF` (`--cap 1 --spare 1`): one
  `viola verify --record`; only verify's compiled pastes are typed; NO key and NO byte into any CLI dialog; the
  sender is verify's own `claude -p` child with its one tool; the kept stamp and the record stay under
  `target/live-rig/`.
- **The second base start (`HG`, `--cap 2`) opens ONLY IF `S1` read red on the `identity-floor` row for an unknown
  name ALONE — every other row green, `cross-session-prefix` among them.** Then implement STOPS and reports the
  unknown NAMES (names only): the overseer brings them to the founder, he classifies each, the code is mended
  through the revision door, and only that revision's round fires `HG`. A red of any other cause — the
  cross-session row (`no-prompt`, `unprefixed`, a sender that could not load its tool), another row, a scrub
  refusal — is a finding: implement stops and no start follows it.
- **The spare (`HF-2`) is spent only on a start the rig refuses before its ledger line or a host CONTENDED by a
  neighbour** — never on a red reading. A third base start is the founder's.
- **Nothing is written under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`.** `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is READ once per
  start by the rig (a 0600 copy, removed on every exit path). `~/.viola/ledger/stamps.json` is read for its sha
  alone and must read unmoved. The pinned product is not rebuilt, replaced or re-pinned.
- **No VALUE of any environment variable is printed, logged or reported — names only,** in your messages too.
- Each start is ledgered with the clock's time (`date -u`) BEFORE it is made.

## The host

- Run nothing heavier than this chunk's own gate entries. Read `df` before any step that rebuilds whole.
- **Before `S1`:** read `python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py
  read --last 15`. A CONTENDED reading that names a NEIGHBOUR makes no start: stop and say so in one line — the
  overseer arranges a quiet window and sends the word to go on. A QUIET reading goes on with no word needed.
- A gate red where no assertion failed on a value (a stall, a timeout, a kill) is read against the same record
  first and never re-run for green into a contended host: say so and wait for the overseer's word.

## Stops

- **The plan's order is the order.** Both rows' fake-agent cases, the canary-value test, the keep-the-red case and
  every control are green before the round. A control's record names the guard's OWN case as failed and lists by
  name any other case failing in it.
- **A RED `S1` stops implement BEFORE the landing and the operator pass,** with the start's own words: which row
  read `fail` and its closed word, whether the sender's prompt arrived, the unknown names if any (names only), a
  `--record` refusal with its closed code. Nothing is retried on a red reading.
- An after-read that does not hold (the kept stamp short of 29, the live stamp moved, a name diff other than the
  expected lines) stops before the landing.
- A red that would move a plan entry stops implement before the operator pass: say which entry and why.
- The WATCH on `cli_wheel path5_a_turn_left_running_is_cleared_by_pause_then_release` is read at each run from
  the test's own line; a recurrence is read from the job log and the test's own events BEFORE any mend, and a CI
  red on it is recorded and NOT re-run before the overseer's word.
- A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and say so. On an account-limit
  refusal, stop where you are. Remove no scratch clone by a recursive delete: name it in the report.
- The rig keeps its frames, the record and the kept stamp locally until the landing copies the record; nothing of
  the operator's status line or config enters a commit. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home; no
  test starts a real `claude`. No leaf gains a figure the code states. No master row is reworded in this skill.

## On green

Write the chunk report (P4), then run the operator pass in this same window with the `ci.py conclusion` read
(leg=operator) as usual, and land `evidence/operator-pass.md`. Then stop: the wrap is a fresh window's.
End every process you start.
