title: F. The floor and the non-identity list (`inputs#I10` items 2–3)

data.head: ### F. The floor and the non-identity list (`inputs#I10` items 2–3)

body: F1. **`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`.**

- `IDENTITY_FLOOR: [&str; 13]` adds `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_NOTES_DIR` and `CLAUDE_CODE_LAUNCHED_BY_SESSION_IDS` beside
  the eleven, its doc comment naming the source: the eleven measured on a wrapped host, the two read from the 2.1.328
  bundle as names set beside the session's identity for its children (`red-analysis.md` §A); the sibling unmeasured
  live (`inputs#I10` item 2).
- `NON_IDENTITY_HOOK_NAMES: [&str; 4]` adds `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`.
- A `plan_strip` case shows a kept `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_NOTES_DIR` stripped all the same.

F2. **The strip's oracle, `tests/tui_env_strip.rs`.** `STRIPPED` gains the two floor names, each with a canary value
    of the canary shape (`canary-notes-value-<hex4>`, `canary-launched-value-<hex4>`), and the two canaries join
    `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/secret_scan.rs`'s `CRITICAL` (`(test-plan · decision/canary-list-single-sourced)`;
    `scan_covers_every_canary_the_root_tests_plant`). The test asserts each of the fifteen names (thirteen floor, the
    unknown, none kept) stripped and named, and no value under the home. Keeps tests S1–S4.

12. **Run B's cross-session turn** (`src/cmd/verify/typed/turns.rs` `framing_turns`, `typed/runs.rs`
    `trusted_run`).
    - **Where:** between the `/compact` paste's answer and the `/clear` paste (lean T1). The session id then is
      still `ledger::resume_target`'s (Run B's first SessionStart, `/compact` keeps it), which the same run's agents
      read listed live.
    - **Run B's args** (`trusted_args`, `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs`): the run's own args, then `SETTINGS_FLAG`
      and `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS`, then the plugin dir (F-P4-2 (c), `inputs#I3`). That is the same form
      `dialog_run` uses for `DIALOG_SETTINGS`.
      - It overrides the user's own `crossSessionInbound` and default-mode parity for Run B alone.
      - Managed policy, a repo or local setting that tightens, an invalid value and the CLI's `receive` switch still
        win, and each reads the row `fail` (`founder-forks.md`, «Answer to the overseer's P5 question»).
      - The sender carries no settings.
    - **When it runs:** only when the box guard reads the box up and `resume_target` gives an id.
    - **The sender:** spawned through `run_bounded` with subject `verify-sender`, logged as `run_logged` logs:
      - args: `program_args` + `-p <sender_prompt(id)> --model haiku --no-session-persistence --allowedTools
        SendMessage`. No `--plugin-dir`, no `--settings`;
      - cwd: verify's print-probe dir (`Inputs` at `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs:59` gains `sender_cwd`, the
        `ProbeDir`'s `dir`);
      - the same R8 strip;
      - bound: `SENDER_DEADLINE` (120 s, a new const beside `PROBE_DEADLINE` in verify.rs), stopped by the stop.
    - **The wait:** if the sender exited 0, verify waits for one more UserPromptSubmit up to `CROSS_SESSION_WINDOW`
      (30 s, a compiled bound on viola's own wait), then for its turn's end (`added_turn_ended`) up to the probe
      deadline. A non-zero exit or the deadline skips the wait. No retry inside one verify (`inputs#I2` item 6).
    - **After it:** `rows = run.box_wait(now)`. If the guard reads the box up, `/clear` is pasted as today and Run B
      ends by Ctrl-C as today. If it does not, `/clear` is not pasted and Run B ends by `end_by_kill`, no key
      (lean T2, `(architecture · decision/verify-types-nothing-into-dialogs)`). Every other end of Run B is
      unchanged.

14. **The fake agent** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/agents.rs`; tests S3; security S3).
    All fake-agent-only:
    - **Sender:** a `-p` prompt that opens with `CROSS_SESSION_SENDER_HEAD` is a sender.
      - It reads the id after the head up to the first space.
      - It finds the registry row beside its executable whose `sessionId` is that id and whose process's parent pid
        (`/proc/<pid>/stat`) equals its own parent pid. Concurrent tests share the exe dir and the recorded id.
      - It writes an empty 0600 `<exe dir>/inbox/<that pid>` and exits 0.
      - With no such row, or a set holding no `UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1.json`, it exits 1 and writes nothing.
      - It fires no hook.
    - **Receiver:** under `--framing`, an interactive fake polls `<exe dir>/inbox/<own pid>` on `CONTROL_POLL`, but
      ONLY when its own argv carries `--settings` with a document equal to `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS`. The fake reads
      the flag as the CLI would read the setting. On the inbox file, the fake removes it, fires `UserPromptSubmit`
      variant `cross-session-1` as recorded, then `end_turn(None)`. Without the literal it reads no inbox.
    - **`--cross-session-turn-screen <phase>`:** a new option, parsed beside `--tag-turn-screen`, for step 18's
      kill case alone.
    - **Env replay:** when the set holds `Env.recorded-1.json`, every SessionStart hook child is spawned with each
      `added` name set to the compiled placeholder `FAKE_AGENT_ENV_VALUE` (`fake-agent`). That is how the capture
      arm reads the recorded names over the fake. The fake's own receipts are unchanged
      (`(test-plan · contract/fake-agent-receipt/env)`).
    - **Cases** in `test_cases_modes.rs`:
      - `sender_delivers_only_to_its_siblings_session` — the sender reaches the row of its parent's child alone, and
        exits 1 with no inbox file for another parent's row;
      - `receiver_fires_the_cross_session_variant_once`;
      - `receiver_reads_no_inbox_without_the_accept_settings` — the same inbox file with no `--settings`, or with
        another document, fires nothing and stays in place;
      - `session_start_hook_carries_the_recorded_env_names`.

15. **The test-built synthetic sets** (`tests/support/verify.rs`; committed nowhere, written at test run time like
    `dialog_set`, the precedent `chunks/2026-11-20-permissionrequest-question-answered` step 13b):
    - `framing_set()` gains `UserPromptSubmit.cross-session-1`, a prompt opening `<cross-session-message from=`;
    - a new `write_env_set(fixtures, version, names)` writes `Env.recorded-1.json`.

    Each is named SYNTHETIC in its doc comment and a one-line comment above it. The default names are three floor
    names and `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`.

16. **Unit cases** (ledger test files; rstest tables per tests S2):
    - **`test_cases_checks.rs`:**
      - `cross_session_prefix_passes_on_a_prefixed_arrival`.
      - `cross_session_prefix_fails_when`, in this case order: `case_1_not_run`, `case_2_no_prefix` (`unprefixed`),
        `case_3_no_prompt`, `case_4_sender_failed`, `case_5_sender_deadline`.
      - `identity_floor_passes_on_floor_and_hook_names`.
      - `identity_floor_fails_when`, in this case order: `case_1_unread`, `case_2_unknown_name`,
        `case_3_unshaped_name`.
      - `identity_floor_drops_kept_names_before_the_check`: a kept unknown name passes and is absent from `added`.
    - **`test_cases_stamps.rs`:** `merge_stamp` writes both measured blocks, names and counts only. A 27-row stamp
      reads unverified, and a 29-row one verified. Every relied-count literal moves.
    - **`test_cases.rs`:** the row-count and verdict vectors at 29.
    - **`test_cases_runs.rs`:** `framing_variants` names `cross-session-1`.
    - Every count is swept by `len()` and by the summaries' sums (testing.md 2026-11-19).

18. **The rows' fake-agent cases** (`tests/cli_verify.rs`, over a synthetic set at a test-owned version, tests S3).
    The fake agent is planted by the shared helpers alone (`(test-plan · decision/tests-never-read-host-sessions)`).
    - `cross_session_prefix_reads_pass_over_the_fake_sender`:
      - step line `[28/29] cross-session-prefix … pass`;
      - the stamp's `cross_session_probe` reads `{"outcome":"harness","prefix":"cross-session",…}`;
      - one `verify-sender` process pair;
      - Run B's receipt argv carries `--settings` followed by the literal `CROSS_SESSION_SETTINGS`, and the sender's
        argv carries no `--settings`;
      - the receipt shows `/clear` pasted after the cross-session turn.
    - **The keep-the-red case** (`inputs#I3` item 1), ONE rstest:
      `cross_session_prefix_keeps_its_red_under_the_accept_settings`. In both cases Run B's receipt argv carries the
      literal, the row reads `fail`, exit 1, and `/clear` is pasted, since the box reads up.
      - `case_1_no_prompt_arrives` — the set holds no `cross-session-1` variant, so the fake sender exits 1 and no
        prompt reaches Run B. Outcome `sender-failed`.
      - `case_2_arrives_unprefixed` — the set's synthetic `cross-session-1` prompt opens with plain text. Outcome
        `unprefixed`.

      The sender-exits-0 `no-prompt` path is held at unit level (step 16's `case_3_no_prompt`). Over the fake it
      would wait out the 30 s `CROSS_SESSION_WINDOW`, past the 20 s per-test kill.
    - `cross_session_prefix_ends_run_b_by_kill_when_the_box_is_not_up`:
      - the fake runs with a new option, `--cross-session-turn-screen <phase>`. Like `--tag-turn-screen`
        (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs:183`), it draws a recorded screen after the cross-session turn, here a modal
        screen of the test-built screen set;
      - no Ctrl-C byte in the receipt after the cross-session turn;
      - `/clear` not pasted.
    - `identity_floor_reads_pass_over_the_recorded_env_names`.
    - `identity_floor_reads_fail_on_an_unknown_name`: the env set holds `CLAUDE_VIOLA_TEST_NEW_X`. The step line is
      `fail`, and the stamp's `env_probe.unknown` is `["CLAUDE_VIOLA_TEST_NEW_X"]`.

20. **The rig (test-only, `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`).**
    - **Labels:** `Arm::of_label` maps `HF`, `HF-2` and `HG` to `Arm::VR`.
    - **Kept stamps:** `StampShape::of` gives `HF` and `HF-2` `Keep(FLOOR_STAMP)` (`floor-stamp.json`), and `HG`
      `Keep(FLOOR_STAMP_2)` (`floor-stamp-2.json`). F-P4-1 (a).
    - **Summary lines:** `stamp_lines` (mod.rs:2809) prints four new lines, `unread` when there is no entry:
      - `cross-session-prefix: <word>`;
      - `identity-floor: <word>`;
      - `cross-session: <measured.cross_session_probe.outcome>`, a code word or `unread`;
      - `env-unknown: <count of measured.env_probe.unknown>`.
    - **`FLOOR_ROWS`:** takes both rows, 23 → 25, its rule «every relied row but four» kept
      (`the_floor_rows_are_every_relied_row_but_four`).
    - The doc comments name the labels. The label and stamp-shape tables (mod.rs:3245, :3409) and the `stamp_lines`
      cases take the new rows.

21. **Phase B gates:** entries 8–14 (§Test Commands), then the controls `kept-names-removed`, `floor-unknown-fails`
    and `prefix-match`. All are green and «holds» before the round. The stamped-home suites are not run here (above).

C2. **Before the round, every stamped-home suite reads green at 28 rows.** Over the committed 2.1.328 set the fake
    replays no env record, so a hook child carries no `CLAUDE*` name but a kept one, and `identity-floor` reads
    `pass`; no row needs a variant the set lacks. The one red by construction until the landing is
    `env_fixtures_pass_hygiene` (no committed env record yet), so the E2E layer runs after the landing alone.

25. **A red `S1`.** The founder's rule (`inputs#I2` item 5), applied to the rig summary's own words.
    - **First:** implement records the rig summary whole in `evidence/live-round.md`, closed words only. It fires the
      kept-stamp and env-names after-reads by `--entry`, and they read even on a red.
    - **The one red that opens a second base start:** `identity-floor: fail` with `env-unknown` ≥ 1, `failing:
      identity-floor` alone, every other row `pass` (`cross-session-prefix: pass` among them), and the record not
      refused.
      - Implement stops and hands the `unknown` names (names only) to the overseer for the founder's dialog.
      - He classifies each, onto the floor or onto `NON_IDENTITY_HOOK_NAMES`.
      - The code is mended through the phase's revision door.
      - That revision's round fires `HG` under `--cap 2 --spare 1`, which re-records.
    - **Any other red is a finding:** the cross-session row, another row, a scrub refusal, `env-unknown` 0 with
      `identity-floor: fail` (an unread or unshaped capture). Implement stops and no start follows it.
    - **The spare `HF-2`:** only for a start the rig refuses before its ledger line, or a host read CONTENDED by a
      neighbour. Never for a red reading. A third base start is the founder's.

26. **No key and no byte into any CLI dialog.**
    - The rig types none.
    - Verify types only its compiled pastes, and every probe dialog is answered by the capture hook's closed ids.
    - The sender raises none: print mode, one allowed tool.
    - From the real home, `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is READ once per start by the rig: a 0600 copy, removed on
      every exit path.
    - Nothing is written under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola` (`inputs#I2` item 5;
      `(security-plan · decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty)`).

B1. Entries 1–12 of §Test Commands, in order — all green, and the guard and the census reading `cut: whole` and no
    output — before the round. Then three one-shot controls (§Test Commands prose), each «holds» with the guard's own
    case among the failed ones. A control's record names every other case that failed in it.

28. **`tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`** walks `Env.recorded-1.json` (the env class: `v` 1 and `added`, an array
    of names matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`) and the `cross-session` framing stem.

29. **`tests/contract_fake_agent_drift.rs`.** Its two verify-exit assertions (the precedent's step 25a) expect exit 0
    only on a set holding both `question-permission` and `cross-session` variants. On every other framed set they
    expect exit 1, AND exactly the step lines of the rows that set lacks read `fail`: `permission-request-question`
    and/or `cross-session-prefix`. The summary's fail count equals that number. The byte drift is still compared on
    every set.

- **Phase A** (the capture arm, 27 rows): the formatter, the linter, the root bin's unit cases, the canary test, then
  the workspace unit, integration and E2E layers.

- **Phase B** (the rows): the formatter, the linter, the agent crate's cases (the `floor-unknown-fails` and
  `prefix-match` controls' entry), the rig's library cases, the root bin's unit cases, the rows' `cli_verify` cases
  and the canary test (the `kept-names-removed` control's entry).

- **The round:** the install read, the census, the plain build with its hash, the kept record and stamp absence, the
  live home's stamp sha, the runtime dir owner-only. Then `S1`, then the census keyed `operator`.

- **The after-reads:** the kept stamp at 29, the env names (report-only), the live home's sha unmoved, and the
  record's names against the committed set.
- **After the landing:** the `diff -r`, then the unit, integration and E2E layers, then the boot smoke.
- **The operator pass.**
- No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 8); obs S5's mutation clause is not exercised.

- No release check entry: CI's `release` job runs `scripts/release-check.sh` on the push. The fake agent stays behind
  `fake-agent`.
- No runtime-dir entry: it guarded the sender's sockets, which left the chunk.
- Every test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint; the canary binary sits on the 20 s override.

- The live start runs under the rig's private scratch at `/tmp/viola-rig-<uid>/`, `--deadline 1500` under the entry's
  `timeout`.

The round's guarding probes are its `round` entries ahead of `HG`; none primes anything. `HG` is ledgered in
`.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-20-harness-prefix-and-identity-floor-ledger-rows/evidence/floor-starts.ndjson` (its
first line `HF`'s); `--cap` is the running total of base lines in that file.

The after-reads read `HG`'s kept stamp, which the leg makes: they carry no `artifact`, and stand after the round's
span (a non-leg entry inside it is refused), fired by `--entry` after the round.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries (validation.md check
4 (6)). Each reads «holds» only when its case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line; each fires on a whole-binary entry,
and its record lists by name every case that failed in the removed run. `--timeout 600` each.
| | `kept-names` | `floor-unknown` | `floor-grows` |
- «holds» needs the guard's OWN case among them.

The values guard has no control: the arm never reads a value (step 2's `vars_os().map(|(k, _)| k)`), so no deletion
can make it keep one. The canary test is its proof.
| | `kept-names-removed` | `floor-unknown-fails` | `prefix-match` |
| **File** | `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` | `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` | `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` |

| **The edit removes** | the clause of `env_reading` that removes `kept` from `added` | the clause of the `identity-floor` check that requires `unknown` empty | the two names F1 adds to `IDENTITY_FLOOR` (the array back to eleven) |
| **Case** | `kept_name_reaches_no_stamp_or_record` | `identity_floor_fails_when::case_2_unknown_name` | `tui_env_strip_removes_identity_and_unknown_claude_names` |
| **Fired on** | entry 10 (the canary and strip binaries) | entry 6 (the agent crate) | entry 10 |

# Implement directive — «Harness-prefix and identity-floor ledger rows» (chunk 2026-11-20-harness-prefix-and-identity-floor-ledger-rows)

The REVISED plan is approved (the revision's P5 card 1). Re-enter at its step R1, the unwind. This window is fresh: read the chunk's documents and run dir from disk first. This
directive is the only file of its folder you read or snap.

**In your own chat messages never print a compiled screen literal verbatim**: name it. This session is driven
through the pinned product, which holds none of the last four mends: call no scheduled-wake or timer tool.

## The live cap for THIS chunk, after the red `HF` (the founder's own answers, 2026-11-21; nothing widens it)

- **ONE more base start and the spare still unspent, on the same ledger (`evidence/floor-starts.ndjson`), claude
  2.1.328 by path, under the rig's PRIVATE config and scratch home: `HG` (`--cap 2 --spare 1`)** — one
  `viola verify --record` of the 28-row tree (the identity row alone; the cross-session row and its sender are cut
  by the revised plan); only verify's compiled pastes are typed; NO key and NO byte into any CLI dialog; the kept
  stamp and the record stay under `target/live-rig/`.
- **A RED `HG` of any cause stops implement before the landing; no start follows it** — a further base start is
  the founder's. The spare is spent only on a start the rig refuses before its ledger line or a host CONTENDED by
  a neighbour, never on a red reading.
- **Nothing is written under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`.** `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is READ once per
  start by the rig (a 0600 copy, removed on every exit path). `~/.viola/ledger/stamps.json` is read for its sha
  alone, RE-TAKEN right before `HG`, and must read unmoved after it. The pinned product is not rebuilt, replaced
  or re-pinned. This session runs claude 2.1.330; the start goes against 2.1.328 by path.
- **No VALUE of any environment variable is printed, logged or reported — names only,** in your messages too.
- The start is ledgered with the clock's time (`date -u`) BEFORE it is made.

## The host

- Run nothing heavier than this chunk's own gate entries. Read `df` before any step that rebuilds whole.
- **Before `S1`:** read `python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py
  read --last 15`. A CONTENDED reading that names a NEIGHBOUR makes no start: stop and say so in one line — the
  overseer arranges a quiet window and sends the word to go on. A QUIET reading goes on with no word needed.
- A gate red where no assertion failed on a value (a stall, a timeout, a kill) is read against the same record
  first and never re-run for green into a contended host: say so and wait for the overseer's word.

## Stops

- **The plan's order is the order.** The unwind first; then the identity row's fake-agent cases, the canary-value test and
  every control are green before the round. A control's record names the guard's OWN case as failed and lists by
  name any other case failing in it.
- **A RED `S1` stops implement BEFORE the landing and the operator pass,** with the start's own words: which row
  read `fail` and its closed word, whether the sender's prompt arrived, the unknown names if any (names only), a
  `--record` refusal with its closed code. Nothing is retried on a red reading.
- An after-read that does not hold (the kept stamp short of 28, the live stamp moved, a name diff other than the
  expected lines) stops before the landing.
- A red that would move a plan entry stops implement before the operator pass: say which entry and why.
- The WATCH on `cli_wheel path5_a_turn_left_running_is_cleared_by_pause_then_release` is read at each run from
  the test's own line; a recurrence is read from the job log and the test's own events BEFORE any mend, and a CI
  red on it is recorded and NOT re-run before the overseer's word.
- A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and say so. On an account-limit
  refusal, stop where you are. Remove no scratch clone by a recursive delete: name it in the report.
- The rig keeps its frames, the record and the kept stamp locally until the landing copies the record; nothing of
  the operator's status line or config enters a commit. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home; no
  test starts a real `claude`. No leaf gains a figure the code states. No master row is reworded in this skill.

## On green

Write the chunk report (P4), then run the operator pass in this same window with the `ci.py conclusion` read
(leg=operator) as usual, and land `evidence/operator-pass.md`. Then stop: the wrap is a fresh window's.
End every process you start.

## 2026-11-20-harness-prefix-and-identity-floor-ledger-rows — 4. Span / Trace Coverage: 1 row(s)
**Section:** 4. Span / Trace Coverage
**Change:** ~ decision/identity-floor-always-stripped · rule: was «The 11 names of the identity floor are always removed whatever the persistent set says; beyond the floor there is no compile-time list of known names.»; now «Every identity-floor name is always removed whatever the persistent set says; beside the floor stands a compile-time list of known non-identity hook names, which the floor never strips.»
**Why:** decision/identity-floor-always-stripped: The standing row's count of 11 and its «beyond the floor there is no compile-time list of known names» are false since the floor grew and NON_IDENTITY_HOOK_NAMES was built; fit read the named list as an inventory. — resolved (Q1), PROVISIONAL: delegate the overseer, 2026-11-21, inputs#I15: «Confirm (Recommended)»
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-21T08-50-56Z-wrap/

- `ledger` module (as landed, pure, no I/O): `LedgerRow`, its closed rows (the members of `LedgerRow::ALL`, in its order) `shim-resolution` · `spine-hooks` · `session-start-fields` · `prompt-verbatim` · `stop-message` · `largest-hook-payload` · `modal-signature` · `input-box-signature` · `quiet-period` · `confirm-window` · `question-answer` · `plan-approve-revise` · `question-notes` · `dialog-concurrency` · `long-paste-wrapper` · `tag-escaping` · `local-command-clear` · `paste-newline` · `resume-session` · `agents-join` · `local-command-compact` · `local-command-echo` · `local-command-context` (relied; `/context` writes its stdout tag to the transcript and submits no prompt within the confirmation window) · `trust-record` (probed by `viola verify`'s Run F, after Run E: passes only when the trust record was written, Run A showed the trust modal, and Run F's start shows no modal and the input box) · `browser-tools-prompt` (relied; `pass` when some verify run's first screen is the CLI's browser-tools prompt, `absent` when no run met it, `fail` when any first screen reads none; the one relied row whose `absent` counts toward verified) · `identity-floor` (relied; passes when every CLAUDE name the CLI adds to a SessionStart hook is an identity-floor name or a known non-identity name, fails on an unknown name or an unread or off-shape env-names file, kept names dropped before the check; its probe stamped as `measured.env_probe`, names only); the relied set `LedgerRow::relied()` (every row of `ALL`, in its order); (no status-line capture, variant or shell verdict: viola intercepts no status line); `resume_target` (Run E's target id: the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture, only when `is_session_id` accepts it) and `resume_variants` (`SessionStart.resume-1.json`); `AgentsCapture` / `agents_variant` (Run B's agents capture and its `Agents.recorded-1.json` filter); `TypedRun`, `Probes { print, typed, trusted, dialogs, resumed, agents }` (`trusted`: Run B's captures in claim order; `resumed`: Run E's captures in claim order; `agents`: Run B's one agents capture, an `AgentsCapture`, on which `agents-join` passes only when it parses and holds exactly one row whose `pid` is Run B's child pid, whose `sessionId` is the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture and whose status is idle or busy (`agents_joined`), and fails with no capture; the `local-command-compact` row passes only when the first SessionStart capture of source `compact` after the newline turn's prompt (`compact_start`) has a non-empty `session_id` equal to that of Run B's first SessionStart capture, no UserPromptSubmit carries `/compact`, and `compact_latency_ms` is within `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (`local_command_compacted`)); Run B's compiled paste texts (the eighth `/context`, the `local-command-context` row's probe, a failing read of it `fail`, never `absent`; the seventh `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent`, on which `local-command-echo` passes only on a new stdout tag with no UserPromptSubmit within the confirmation window, the paste skipped and the row failing with no readable transcript; `PROBE_PROMPT`, `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE` (113 bytes, ASCII, exactly one LF at neither end, no CR) and `PROBE_COMPACT_COMMAND` (the list's `/compact`) among them); `FRAMING_TURNS` (in paste order `paste-1` · `paste-2` · `paste-3` · `compact-1` · `clear-1`) and `framing_stem`; `CAPTURE_EVENTS`; `parse_version` (first line exactly `X.Y.Z (Claude Code)`); `capture_plugin_files` (plugin `viola-verify-probe`, four exec-form `--capture` hooks); `check(row, &Probes)`, `largest`; `merge_stamp` (writes `measured.typed_probe`), `verified` (every row of `LedgerRow::relied()` `pass`, or `absent` on `browser-tools-prompt` alone, every one on every build (`local-command-echo`, `trust-record` and `local-command-context` among them, so a stamp of the older, shorter row set written before chunk 2026-11-16-local-command-delivery reads unverified), a stamp holding a retired ledger row verifying on the relied rows alone; a stamp holding exactly the seventeen ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row holds, or exactly the eighteen ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows holds, or exactly the twenty-one ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows holds, or exactly the twenty-two ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board holds, or exactly the twenty-three ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row holds, all `pass`, reads unverified; so every home stamped before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row reads `cli_verified:false` until its next `viola verify`); `scrub`, `is_clean` (reads through `unclean`), `signature_rows`, `screen_is_clean`, `screen_fault` → `ScreenFault { row, seam, why }`, `unclean` → the closed `Unclean` codes `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`. `verified` returns `Result<bool, AgentError>`: a wrong-shaped envelope is `AgentError::StampsMalformed` ("the capability stamps are malformed"). `AgentError` sits at the crate root and also holds `resolve_program`'s one refusal, `ProgramNotFound`, with a fixed message (arch [Error Handling]). `resolve_program` returns `Result<PathBuf, AgentError>`, in the crate and in the root wrapper `src/run/mod.rs`.

- R8 (`plan_strip`, names only): every inherited `CLAUDE*` name (matched exactly) is removed unless it is in `config.json` `claude_env_keep`; an `IDENTITY_FLOOR` name is removed regardless, even when the persistent environment defines it. Logged as `env_stripped_count` + `env_stripped_known` + `env_kept` — never values; only `viola verify`, and the `viola run` and `viola revive` start, read the value of `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, only when `claude_env_keep` keeps that name, to locate the Claude config file.

The `viola` binary. It holds the clap 4.6.7 dispatch (`src/main.rs`, one module per subcommand in `src/cmd/`) and the `run` wrapper (`src/run/`): the PTY pump, the wheel, the readiness-gate wiring and the channel server dispatch. It also owns the pinned copy + plugin write-out, the obs init (`viola::obs`: `MillisUtc`, `viola_obs_init`, the panic hook, the detail writer, the catch-site reporter `report_internal_error`; `open_role_file` and `write_detail` run `strict::check_diagnostics` on an existing `diagnostics/` folder and on the role or detail file before `ensure_private_dir` narrows anything — a symbolic link refused, a folder to the read rule, a file to the read rule, an absent path passing — and a refusal is a failed open: the writer ends at `std::io::sink`, a detail line is dropped) and the human/`--json` output modules (the `human` module: `src/human.rs`, with its phases under `src/human/` — mirror, escape, board, style (the colour layer: `Depth`, `Tokens`, `Facts`, `decide`, `read`), wait, verbs, hints —; `src/human.rs` holds the stderr refusal writer `write_refusal` behind `refuse`, the stderr `write_internal_error` (`error: internal error\n`) behind `internal_error`, and the stdout `write_result` behind `result`, each one `write_all`; called by `run`, `revive`, `verify`, `send`, `wait`, `last`, `list`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `plugin install` and the `main` catch site; no print macro, no `#[allow]`). `viola verify` (`src/cmd/verify.rs`) drives the one print-mode probe and then the six interactive PTY runs (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` and its children under `src/cmd/verify/typed/`: Run A untrusted in an OS-temp dir, Run B trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/` with compiled pastes — the probe prompt, then the long text, the tag-like text, the newline text (`PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE`, 113 bytes, one inner LF), `/compact` (`PROBE_COMPACT_COMMAND`), `/clear` and `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent` (the `local-command-echo` row's probe, passing on a new stdout tag with no UserPromptSubmit within the confirmation window; with no readable transcript the paste skipped and the row failing), then eighth `/context` (the relied `local-command-context` row's probe, passing on a new stdout tag with no UserPromptSubmit within the confirmation window; a failing read of it is `fail`, never `absent`), each added one only into a settled input box, waited for after an added text turn and after the `/compact` turn up to `PROBE_DEADLINE` (`box_wait`: 2.1.287 shows a paste hint in the input-box literal's place for 8.0 s after a long paste) — and, once its first turn has settled and before its framing pastes, ONE `claude agents --json` read (`typed::turns::agents_read`: Run B's program, cwd the probe dir, the R8 strip, `VERSION_DEADLINE`, none once a stop is read; its capture kept in memory, never written to the captures dir; no live start added; in CI the fake agent's `agents` mode answers it), Run C's dialogs in `-dialogs/`, Run D's plan in `-plan/`, then Run E trusted in `-resume/`, resuming Run B's first session with `--resume <id>` (`viola_agent_claude::resume_args(id, false)`, the id Run B's first SessionStart `session_id` through `ledger::resume_target`; empty input, no `--settings`, ended by a kill), then last Run F, after Run E, starting in an untrusted folder for which verify wrote a trust record (the `trust-record` row passing only when the record was written, Run A showed the trust modal, and Run F's start shows no modal and the input box; verify writes that record for its own temp folder only into the Claude config file its child reads, located through `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only when `claude_env_keep` keeps it, never creating an absent file, and removes that one record after; `run`'s and `revive`'s start, on a verified CLI, write the trust record of an untrusted spawn folder); no key into any dialog — the hidden `hook --capture --answers` arm in `src/cmd/hook.rs` answers C and D's from `PROBE_ANSWERS`), checks the relied ledger rows (`check_rows` walks `LedgerRow::relied()`: every row of `LedgerRow::ALL` on every build, the relied `local-command-echo` among them; the relied identity-floor row passing when every CLAUDE name the CLI adds to a SessionStart hook, kept names dropped first, is an identity-floor or known non-identity name, and failing on an unknown name or an unread or off-shape env-names file), prints the step lines (each `pass`, `absent` or `fail`) and `stamped` summary (its pass count including an absent `browser-tools-prompt`, the one relied row whose `absent` counts toward verified) and writes the stamps through `viola_state::stamps::update_stamps` (its `StampsError::StrictModes` refusal printing the home-state pair, exit 1); before its `cli` log opens it runs `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree(home, None, None)` (the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/`, each that exists), a refusal printing the home pair and exiting 1 with no step line, no summary and no line; a verify stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`cmd::verify::stop`: `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`, installed by `viola verify` alone, its handler only setting one process-global flag that every wait of the run reads) kills and reaps the running child with no key, starts no later run, writes no stamp and exits 1 (`unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI`, stdout empty), its drop guards removing only the dirs, and its own trust record from the Claude config file, that run created; SIGKILL, a crash and a failed handler install keep the OS default and leave the dirs to be removed by hand; `run::version_gate` reads them at `run` start. The panic detail backtrace is raw, never-symbolised frames (`src/panic_frames.rs`). It is the only crate with anyhow (dispatch edge and the catch-site reporter) and tracing-subscriber, and it consumes only normalised events.

- `hook <event> --capture <DIR>` (hidden) is `verify`'s capture arm: no `VIOLA_*` and no environment value read, no obs init, no channel, raw 0600 write (on SessionStart alone also `Env.<k>.json` owner-only beside the payload: the CLAUDE names of its own process, every other name only counted, no value ever read or written), exit 0 always.

**What breaks:** started from inside a Claude session, the child inherits `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, the Remote Control bridge and the messaging socket/token (the identity-floor names).
**How to avoid:** the R8 rule: `viola-agent-claude::plan_strip` removes every inherited `CLAUDE*` name matched exactly, except a name in `config.json` `claude_env_keep`, and always every `IDENTITY_FLOOR` name (beside the floor stands a compiled list of known non-identity hook names, which the floor never strips); log names only (`env_stripped_count` / `env_stripped_known` / `env_kept`), never values.
**References:** brief §4.1 S6; arch Occupied Resources → Environment variables; security Decisions Log 2026-09-25; obs D-34.

- `viola verify [--record <dir>] [-- <program> [args…]]` — drive one print-mode probe (Haiku) and six interactive PTY runs (Run A untrusted in an OS-temp dir, Run B trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/` with compiled pastes (the probe prompt, a long text, a tag-like text, a text holding one inner LF, `/compact`, `/clear`, then `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent`, the local-command-echo row's probe, skipped with that row failed when no transcript is readable, then `/context`, the local-command-context row's probe, a failing read of it `fail`, never `absent`) and one `claude agents --json` read once its first turn has settled, before the added pastes (held in memory, spawn pair `agents-probe`, no start added; in CI the fake agent's `agents` mode answers it), Run C's dialogs in `-dialogs/`, Run D's plan in `-plan/`, then Run E in `-resume/` resuming Run B's first session with `--resume <id>` (input empty, no `--settings`), then Run F in an untrusted temp folder whose trust record verify writes into the Claude config file its child reads (never creating an absent file; a run or revive start writes a record only for its own untrusted spawn folder, on a verified CLI), passing the trust-record row only when the record was written, Run A showed the trust modal and Run F's start shows no modal and the input box; no key into any dialog — the probe hook answers C and D's) against the CLI (default `claude`), check the relied ledger rows (`LedgerRow::relied()`, on every build), print `[NN/MM]` step lines ending `pass`, `absent` or `fail` (`absent` on the browser-tools-prompt row alone, when no run met the CLI's browser-tools prompt; `MM` the relied count; the last `[MM/MM] browser-tools-prompt …`) + the `stamped <ver>  <n> pass  <m> fail` summary on stdout (`<n>` counting every relied row that counts toward verified, an absent browser-tools-prompt among them) and write `ledger/stamps.json`; exit 1 on a failing row; exit 1 with the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, no step line, no summary and no log line when `check_home_tree` refuses its home, `ledger/`, `bin/` or `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens (and the same pair, exit 1, after the step lines, when `update_stamps` refuses `ledger/stamps.json`, with `detail:"strict-modes-failed"` on its `process-exit` under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`); a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM kills its child with no key, removes only the probe dirs it created and its own trust record from the Claude config file, writes no stamp, leaves stdout empty, prints `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI` and exits 1 (SIGKILL, a crash or a failed handler install leaves the dirs to remove by hand). `--record <dir>` also writes the scrubbed `<dir>/<ver>/<Event>.default.json` fixtures, the `<Event>.<stem>-<n>.json` dialog variants, Run B's `paste-<n>` / `compact-<n>` / `clear-<n>` framing variants, Run E's first SessionStart as `SessionStart.resume-1.json`, Run B's agents read as `Agents.recorded-1.json` (Run B's own row only), the env-names fixture `Env.recorded-1.json` (names only, never a value: `v` 1 plus `added`) and signature-only `Screen.<phase>.json` screens (a footer or modal row whole, the input box's rule row as its rule chars alone and its prompt row as the prompt char alone, every other row empty; a box whose live prompt row holds a home path, the username or an email refuses the recording) when 0 rows fail; an unclean recording is refused naming the file and check code. A hidden `--record-first-screens`, absent from `--help` and passed only by the live rig, makes a failed `--record` verify write a first-screen file of whole scrubbed rows per run short of the input box (Run A's trust excepted), refused whole when unclean, kept locally and never committed. Run it from a folder you trust in Claude Code whose external CLAUDE.md import is answered. Against the real CLI: local only, spends tokens; CI runs it only against the fake agent's `-p/--print` mode and its `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root --dialogs --framing --transcript --trust-config` interactive modes, under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only and named to the fake agent by `--trust-config` (every stamping verify passes `--transcript` beside `--framing`, or Run B's echo probe is skipped and the local-command-echo row fails). The `Mcp.<variant>.json` MCP exchanges are recorded not by `--record` but by the test-only `viola-mcp-tap` (`record` / `fixture`, the same scrub and closed refusal codes; architecture §Occupied Resources → Binary); the recorded Hyprland replies likewise by the test-only `viola-hypr-tap`, under the same scrub

- Stamps file: `ledger/stamps.json` in the Ledger stamps envelope `{"v":1,"written_at","writer":"verify","data":{"versions":{"<ver>":{"verified_at","rows":{…},"measured":{…}}}}}` (arch §Standard Contracts; `measured.env_probe` holds the identity-floor probe's `read`, `added`, `unknown`, `other_count` and `unshaped`, names only, every kept name removed); a version is verified only when its stamp holds every relied row (`LedgerRow::relied()`, on every build) `pass`, or `absent` on `browser-tools-prompt` alone: a seventeen-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row reads unverified (`cli_verified:false`) until the next `viola verify`, and so does an eighteen-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, a twenty-one-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows, a twenty-two-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board , a twenty-three-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row or a twenty-two-row stamp written before chunk 2026-11-17-trust-record-ledger-row; a stamp's `rows` maps each row id to `pass` or `fail`, browser-tools-prompt may also read `absent`, and trust-record holds the trust writer's code word instead when no record was written

- The statusline arm is removed (chunk 2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed): `viola hook statusline` is an unknown hook event that prints nothing; `hook_event` has ten closed names, the `statusline-shell` subject, `shell_exit_status`, the `hook.statusline` / `statusline.shell_out` spans and the `statusline_command` are gone. The one hidden capture arm, `hook <event> --capture`, initialises no observability and writes no lines; its env-names file, like the strip, every log and the verify stamp and record, carries environment variable names only, never values.

- Harness origin (Decisions Log `2026-09-29`, a boundary widening the founder ratified live): the compiled harness prefixes are four — `<agent-message from=`, `<task-notification>`, `<\cross-session-message`, `<cross-session-message` — matched on the prompt's raw start, and the wrapper relabels a keyless human-filed prompt told as a CLI-scheduled wake origin harness; the escaped cross-session form is the one escaped tag that classifies, so a human typing it at a prompt's start is filed `harness` (accepted side effect). As measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host (chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host) a real cross-session message arrived unescaped and was filed `harness` by the plain prefix, and a `<task-notification>` typed at a prompt's start arrives as typed, so it is filed `harness` too; the escaped injection form stays a relayed measurement and a compiled prefix. That reading and a names-only list of a 2.1.287 hook's `CLAUDE*` environment (12 names; the hook-added `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` are known, not identity names, stand off the identity floor and are read only by verify's env reading) were two one-off scratch measurements on the founder's live answers of 2026-10-07T09:43Z, relayed by the overseer; neither answer covers a second message, a verify child or another probe.

- Test homes on the Linux dev host (the founder's live answer, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, relayed by the overseer; a boundary widening): `target/e2e-home` is a link to the per-user tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>`, so the fixture chain's sweep and drop and harness `cleanup` create and delete outside the working directory, each only a dir the test side itself made (by its owner record, its own temp dir or its session name prefix) or another build's stamp dir whose lock it takes with try_lock. The two keepers follow a linked base only when its target is absolute and one `lstat` reads a real directory with no group or other bit, and refuse a backing whose filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), each refusal a fixed message that names no path (the headroom one holds the two counts); they create it 0700 and remove nothing. `viola` never names the backing; no CI runner has the link. Accepted residual (a live round of `viola plugin install`): the round runs the CLI's own four commands (`claude plugin marketplace add` / `install` / `uninstall` / `marketplace remove`) at `--scope local`, a fresh count of four per rig, from a `proj/` that is its own git repo outside this work tree (on the e2e-home tmpfs, no ancestor `CLAUDE.md`): the CLI takes the local scope's project from the git work tree root, and a `proj/` inside the work tree meets the external-imports dialog after the trust dialog; the rig passes the folder-trust dialog by keys into its own pty only, never a desktop key, on the founder's own word anew for each chunk and by a closed argv grant (on a read screen at most 2 arrows toward the trust row and 1 Enter only when that row reads selected, one x and one DEL only in a ready box, any other key writing nothing; the founder's word binds the grant alone, and the rig's stop, Ctrl-C into its own pty or a no-key group kill, needs no word; on a wrapped start the keys move the wheel to the human, and `viola release <name>` precedes the driver's send); the CLI's writes are its own — its trust entry in `~/.claude.json` for each `proj/` whose dialog was accepted, the session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`, and after the removal its orphaned plugin cache `~/.claude/plugins/cache/viola/viola/<version>/` (re-written in place by a later install and uninstall), `installed_plugins.json` and `known_marketplaces.json` back as before (as measured on claude 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings); viola itself writes nothing under `~/.claude` or into `~/.claude.json`, save `viola verify`'s own trust record for its fresh temp folder in the Claude config its child reads, only that record removed after (a SIGKILL leaves it); on a verified CLI only, `run` and `revive`'s start set `hasTrustDialogAccepted` alone (every other key kept) in the trust record of an untrusted spawn folder in the config its child reads, never for the user home folder or a folder the CLI's own walk reads as trusted, and that record stays. Accepted residual (a scratch footer reading of a newer CLI): one `viola run` start of the CLI under a tmpfs `--home`, in a detached 80×24 pane, its cwd a fresh `.viola-footer-<pid>/` under the repository root, with no key typed; one `viola list` read against that home; at two instants the pane's bottom three screen rows, scrubbed of the home and the user word, written to the chunk's `evidence/`, never a row above the footer; then the start is killed and its cwd removed; it left no transcript under `~/.claude/projects/` (as measured on 2.1.302 at chunk 2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows). It is no product path and no standing permission: another such reading needs its own answer. The live rig runs its child under a private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in its own scratch, seeded only with keys whose values come from the CLI bundle's own logic, none read from the user's config (used-config markers and, on every arm but VP, the browser-tools prompt turned off; VP leaves the browser-tools key out), with an environment built from a closed kept list of host names plus its own, and reads the user's `~/.claude.json` only after a moved stamp, searching it for rig-made needles, dropping the bytes and keeping one closed word; the VH arm runs under the real home and config, reads no credentials, keeps only key names and one needle word, prints no value, and needs an explicit home, Claude dir and user config. The live rig may read whether the key name `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled` stands in its own private scratch config, printing written or absent, and never reads a value (a boundary widening, answered for the rig alone). The live rig's MCP recording arm keeps no CLI output (stdout drained and dropped, stderr kept only as a byte count and a SHA), and its MCP config is a private 0600 file inside the scratch, removed with it. The live rig's CX arm reads the session transcript through `MAX_FRAME`, counting only tags past the kept length and keeping no byte of it, and sends only through `viola send` under the rig's private config. A live session's screen frames are kept only under a gitignored local path, never in a work dir, a run dir or a commit; what lands is a closed-word summary per frame. The live rig copies the claude OAuth credentials file owner-only into its private scratch, reads only its expiry, refuses a start with under 20 minutes of token, removes the copy on every exit path, and writes no credential, host path or config value into any ledger, frame or summary; the VH arm, run under the real home, makes no copy and reads no credentials file. The live rig keeps a stamp from its CS, WS, PQ, HF or HG scratch home owner-only and no-clobber and seeds it only into its own CC or R3W scratch home; CC with no kept stamp refuses before its ledger line and before any scratch, R3W before its ledger line. The live rig's SF arm runs the real claude inside a network-closed bwrap sandbox with its own network namespace; an absent or failing sandbox, or one sharing the rig's namespace, refuses the arm with `refused: sandbox`, exit 3, uncounted, before any credentials read or ledger line. The live rig's R3W arm reads from the events log in its own scratch home only viola's own wheel lines and the prompt's origin word, and records the captured prompt's key names, never their values. The live rig's config-top reading keeps only the top-level names of its private claude config and their regular-file counts (a name outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,40}` reads as other) and reads no file content. The live rig's HB arm types one x and one DEL into a fresh box in its own unwrapped pty before any send, and records only cell attributes and counts, never screen text.
